column7: To the left of the formula bar, showing the current cell address
column8: At the bottom of the screen, showing sheet tabs
column9: In the Home tab, under the "Cells" group
column10: In the View tab, under "Zoom" options
column14: Name Box is located to the left of the formula bar

column6: In MS Word, the status bar at the bottom of the screen displays:
column8: Page number, word count, language, and zoom controls
column9: Only the current font name and size
column10: The full file path of the document
column14: Status bar shows page number, word count, language, and zoom

column6: In a typical network topology diagram, a star topology is characterized by:
column7: All devices connected to a single central hub/switch
column8: Devices connected in a circular ring
column9: Each device connected to exactly two other devices forming a linear path
column10: All devices connected to a common backbone cable
column14: Star topology = all devices connected to a central hub/switch

column5: Introduction to Financial Accounting and its terms
column6: Which of the following is the correct accounting equation?
column14: The fundamental accounting equation states that Assets = Capital + Liabilities (or Assets = Liabilities + Owner's Equity). This equation must always balance.

column5: Introduction to Financial Accounting and its terms
column6: In the books of a trader, goods taken away for personal use are credited to:
column14: When goods are withdrawn for personal use, the Purchases Account is credited (to reduce purchases) and Drawings Account is debited. This is because the goods were originally recorded as purchases.

column5: Elements of Double entry Book Keeping
column6: Which of the following is NOT a subsidiary book?
column14: The Ledger is the principal book of accounts, not a subsidiary book. Subsidiary books include Cash Book, Purchase Book, Sales Book, Purchase Return Book, Sales Return Book, and Journal Proper.

column5: Elements of Double entry Book Keeping
column6: A debit note is sent by:
column14: A debit note is sent by the buyer to the seller when goods are returned or when an allowance is claimed. It informs the seller that the buyer's account has been debited.

column6: The process of transferring entries from Journal to Ledger is called:
column14: Posting is the process of transferring entries from the Journal (book of original entry) to the Ledger (book of final entry). Balancing is done after posting.

column6: Which of the following accounts normally has a debit balance?
column14: Purchases Account normally has a debit balance as it represents an expense. Creditors and Bank Loan are liabilities (credit balance), and Rent Received is income (credit balance).

column6: Outstanding wages is an example of:
column14: Outstanding wages is a Representative Personal Account because it represents a person or group to whom wages are payable. It is not a real or nominal account.

column6: If the trial balance tallies, it indicates:
column8: Mathematical accuracy of posting is established
column14: A tallied trial balance only confirms mathematical accuracy (equal debits and credits). It does not guarantee absence of errors like errors of omission, commission, or principle.

column6: A Triple Column Cash Book contains columns for:
column14: A Triple Column Cash Book has three columns on each side: Cash, Bank, and Discount. It records cash transactions, bank transactions, and cash/bank discounts simultaneously.

column6: When a cheque received from a customer is dishonored, it is recorded in:
column9: Bank column on the debit side
column10: Bank column on the credit side
column14: A dishonored cheque is recorded on the credit side of the Cash Book in the bank column because the bank balance decreases when the cheque is returned unpaid.

column6: Bank Reconciliation Statement is prepared to reconcile:
column7: Cash Book and Pass Book balances
column9: Trading Account and Profit & Loss Account
column14: BRS is prepared to reconcile the difference between the balance as per Cash Book and the balance as per Pass Book (Bank Statement) due to timing differences or errors.

column6: Direct deposits made by customers into the bank, not yet recorded in Cash Book, will require:
column14: Direct deposits by customers increase the Pass Book balance but not the Cash Book. To reconcile, the Cash Book balance needs to be increased (added) as it was understated.

column6: A cheque issued but not yet presented for payment results in:
column7: Higher balance in Pass Book than Cash Book
column8: Lower balance in Pass Book than Cash Book
column14: When a cheque is issued, the Cash Book is credited immediately, but the Pass Book is debited only when presented. Thus, Pass Book shows a higher balance until presentation.

column6: Trading Account is prepared to ascertain:
column14: The Trading Account is prepared to calculate Gross Profit or Gross Loss by matching direct revenues (sales) against direct costs (cost of goods sold).

column6: Which of the following is NOT a direct expense?
column14: Office Rent is an indirect expense recorded in the Profit and Loss Account. Wages, Factory Rent, and Carriage Inward are direct expenses recorded in the Trading Account.

column6: Closing stock is valued at:
column7: Cost Price or Market Price, whichever is higher
column8: Cost Price or Market Price, whichever is lower
column14: As per the conservatism principle, closing stock is valued at Cost Price or Market Price (Net Realizable Value), whichever is lower, to avoid overstating assets.

column5: Profit Loss Account and Balance Sheet
column6: Prepaid insurance is shown in the Balance Sheet as:
column14: Prepaid insurance represents insurance paid in advance for future periods. It is a current asset because it provides economic benefit within 12 months.

column5: Profit Loss Account and Balance Sheet
column6: Return inward is deducted from:
column14: Return inward (Sales Return) is deducted from Sales in the Trading Account to arrive at Net Sales. It reduces the total revenue from sales.

column6: Goodwill is a/an:
column14: Goodwill is an intangible asset representing the reputation and customer relations of a business. It has no physical existence but has monetary value.

column6: A, B, and C are partners sharing profits in the ratio 3:2:1. C retires. The new profit-sharing ratio between A and B will be:
column14: Unless otherwise agreed, the remaining partners continue in their old ratio. A and B originally shared 3:2, so after C's retirement, they continue in the same 3:2 ratio.

column6: Fixed cost per unit:
column14: Fixed cost per unit increases when production decreases because the same total fixed cost is spread over fewer units. Total fixed cost remains constant.

column6: Which of the following is NOT a technique of Cost Accounting?
column14: Financial Accounting is a separate branch of accounting, not a technique of Cost Accounting. Standard Costing, Marginal Costing, and Budgetary Control are cost accounting techniques.

column6: A budget prepared for a single level of activity is called:
column14: A Fixed Budget (or Static Budget) is prepared for a single planned level of activity and does not change with actual activity levels. A Flexible Budget adjusts to different activity levels.

column6: The Public Financial Management System (PFMS) is primarily used for:
column8: Monitoring of government funds and expenditure
column14: PFMS is a web-based online software application developed by the Controller General of Accounts (CGA) to monitor government funds and track expenditure in real-time.

column5: Concept of Social Accounting, Social Audit and cash based system of accounting
column6: Under the cash-based system of accounting, revenue is recognized when:
column14: In the cash-based system, revenue is recognized only when cash is actually received, and expenses are recognized only when cash is actually paid, regardless of when earned or incurred.

column5: Concept of Social Accounting, Social Audit and cash based system of accounting
column6: Social Accounting primarily focuses on:
column8: Measurement of social costs and benefits
column14: Social Accounting measures the social costs and benefits of business activities, including impact on employees, community, and environment, beyond just financial profits.

column6: The Voucher Approach in Accounting emphasizes:
column8: Verifiable documentary evidence for every transaction
column14: The Voucher Approach requires every transaction to be supported by a verifiable voucher or documentary evidence (invoice, receipt, etc.) before being recorded in the books.

column6: Which of the following is NOT an objective of Financial Audit?
column14: Preparation of budgets is a management function, not an objective of financial audit. Audit objectives include verifying financial statements, detecting fraud/errors, and ensuring compliance with standards.

column6: Which of the following is a feature of the Indian Financial Management System (IFMS)?
column7: It is used only for state-level transactions
column8: It integrates budgeting, accounting, and expenditure management at both Central and State levels
column9: It replaces the Public Financial Management System (PFMS) entirely
column10: It is exclusively designed for foreign exchange management
column14: The Indian Financial Management System (IFMS) is an integrated financial management information system that combines budgeting, accounting, and expenditure management functions for both Central and State governments, enabling real-time monitoring and transparency in public finances.

column6: Which development in accounting refers to the integration of environmental costs into financial reporting?
column14: Environmental Management Accounting (EMA) is a recent development in accounting that focuses on identifying, collecting, and analyzing environmental cost information for internal decision-making and external reporting, helping organizations measure and manage their environmental impact alongside financial performance.

column6:
Consider the following pairs: City
I. Maracaibo - Ukraine,
II. Tabriz - Venezuela,
III. Nuuk - Greenland,
IV. Donetsk - Iran. How many of the pairs are correct?
column14: Only pair III (Nuuk-Greenland) is correct. Maracaibo is in Venezuela, Tabriz is in Iran, Donetsk is in Ukraine. So only 1 pair is correct.

column6:
What are the key components of the recently launched Digital Agriculture Mission in India?
I. Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) for Agriculture, i.e. Agristack, Krishi Decision Support System, Comprehensive Soil Fertility, and Profile Maps.
II. Digital General Crop Estimation Survey (DGCES).
III. Support for the Mahalanobis National Crop Forecasting Centre (MNCFC). Identify the correct statements.
column14: The Digital Agriculture Mission includes DPI for Agriculture (Agristack, etc.) and DGCES. MNCFC support is not a key component of this mission. So I and II are correct.

column6:
Match the following and

choose the correct option: Statues
1. Statue of Unity,
2. Statue of Oneness,
3. Statue of Equality. Personalities Associated i. Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, ii. Adi Shankaracharya, iii. Sri Ramanuja Acharya.
column14: Statue of Unity (Sardar Patel), Statue of Oneness (Adi Shankaracharya in Omkareshwar), Statue of Equality (Sri Ramanuja Acharya in Hyderabad). So 1-i, 2-ii, 3-iii is correct.

column6:
Which of the following sites are included in the Tentative List of World Heritage Sites released by UNESCO?
I. Khangchendzonga National Park,
II. Natural Heritage of Varkala,
III. Naga Hill Ophiolite,
IV. Natural Heritage of Tirumala Hills,
V. Meghalayan Age Caves,
VI. Rock Shelters of Bhimbetka.
column7: II, III, IV and V only
column8: I, IV, V and VI only
column9: II, III, IV and V only
column14: Khangchendzonga and Bhimbetka are already World Heritage Sites, not in tentative list. Varkala, Naga Hill Ophiolite, Tirumala Hills, and Meghalayan Age Caves are in the tentative list. So II, III, IV, V are correct.

column6:
Consider the following statements about the Tribal Freedom Fighters:
I. Tilka Majhi mobilized the Pahadia tribe to which he belonged and raided the Company treasury.
II. Sidhu and Kanhu Murmu from the Santhal community led the Santhal in the Hul rebellion.
III. Malati Mem of the Tea-garden community opposed Mahatma Gandhi's satyagraha movement.

Which of the above statements are correct?
column14: I and II are correct. Tilka Majhi led the Pahadia tribe and Sidhu-Kanhu led the Santhal Hul. Malati Mem actually supported Gandhi's movement, not opposed it. So only I and II are correct.

column6:
With reference to the Indian Freedom struggle, consider the following events:
I. Poona Pact (1932),
II. Lord Irwin's declaration (1929),
III. Second Round Table Conference (1931). Arrange them in the correct chronological order.
column14: Lord Irwin's declaration (1929) came first, then Second Round Table Conference (1931), then Poona Pact (1932). So correct order is II-III-I.

column6:
Match the following pairs: Hills
1. Nilgiri Hills,
2. Anaimalai Hills,
3. Mahadeo Hills,
4. Vindhyan Range. Related Regions i. Part of the Satpura Range, ii. Parallel to the Narmada Valley, iii. Junction of Eastern and Western Ghats, iv. The Southern Part of the Western Ghats.
column14: Nilgiri Hills are at the junction of Eastern and Western Ghats (iii). Anaimalai Hills are the southern part of Western Ghats (iv). Mahadeo Hills are part of Satpura Range (i). Vindhyan Range is parallel to Narmada Valley (ii). So 1-iii, 2-iv, 3-i, 4-ii is correct.

column6: The Ten-degree channel separates which two regions?
column14: The Ten-degree channel (10°N latitude) separates the Andaman Islands from the Nicobar Islands in the Bay of Bengal.

column6:
Consider the following statements regarding India's demographic trends:
I. Demographic dividend refers to the economic growth potential arising from a declining dependency ratio, due to a rising working-age population.
II. Demographic winter refers to the economic and social challenges arising from an increasing working-age population and decreasing old-age dependency.
III. India is expected to enjoy its demographic dividend till the mid-21st century, and its realization depends on education, skill development, health, and employment generation.

Which of the above statements are correct?
column14: I and III are correct. Demographic winter refers to declining working-age population and increasing old-age dependency, not increasing working-age population. So II is incorrect.

column6:
Consider the following pairs: Wetlands
I. Kolleru Lake - Tamil Nadu,
II. Tawa Reservoir - Madhya Pradesh,
III. Nanjarayan Bird Sanctuary - Andhra Pradesh,
IV. Sultanpur National Park - Haryana.

How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
column14: Only II and IV are correctly matched. Tawa Reservoir is in Madhya Pradesh and Sultanpur National Park is in Haryana. Kolleru Lake is in Andhra Pradesh (not Tamil Nadu). Nanjarayan Bird Sanctuary is in Tamil Nadu (not Andhra Pradesh). So only 2 pairs are correct.

column6:
Which Koppen climate type is described by the following characteristics?
I. Average monthly temperature rarely falls below 18°C.
II. Annual rainfall exceeds 2000 mm, distributed evenly throughout the year.
III. Humid conditions support dense evergreen forests.
column14: Af (Tropical rainforest) climate has temperatures above 18°C throughout the year, rainfall exceeding 2000 mm evenly distributed, and supports dense evergreen forests. This is the classic description of tropical rainforest climate.

column6:
Which of the following statements about India's National Waterways are correct?
I. National Waterway 2 (NW-2) is the Brahmaputra River stretch from Dhubri to Sadiya in Assam, covering about 891 km.
II. National Waterway 3 (NW-3) is the West Coast Canal, which connects Kollam and Kottapuram in Kerala.
III. National Waterway 97 (NW-97) runs on the Zuari River, connecting Sanvordem Bridge to Marmugao Port.
IV. National Waterways 111 (NW-111) is operational in the Sunderbans Region.
column14: All four statements are correct. NW-2 is Brahmaputra, NW-3 is West Coast Canal in Kerala, NW-97 is on Zuari River in Goa, and NW-111 is in the Sunderbans region of West Bengal.

column6:
According to Kalhana's Rajatarangini, identify the correct sequential order of the following dynasties in the Jammu and Kashmir region:
I. Gonanda dynasty,
II. Utpala dynasty,
III. Karkota Dynasty,
IV. Lohara dynasty.
column14: According to Rajatarangini, the correct order is: Gonanda dynasty (oldest), followed by Karkota Dynasty, then Utpala dynasty, and finally Lohara dynasty. So I-III-II-IV is correct.

column6:
Consider the following statements about Bahu Fort in Jammu:
I. The ancient Bahu Fort in Jammu is believed to have been originally built by Raja Bahu Lochan about 3,000 years ago.
II. It was refurbished by the Dogra rulers in the 19th century.
III. Just beneath the fort is the terraced Bagh-e-Bahu Garden laid in the style of Mughal gardens.

Which of the above statements are correct?
column14: All three statements are correct. Bahu Fort was built by Raja Bahu Lochan, refurbished by Dogra rulers, and Bagh-e-Bahu Garden is in Mughal style below the fort.

column6:
Which Kashmiri art form is described by the following lines?
I. It is a traditional folk theatre style combination of play and dance.
II. It differs from other forms as it features a single performer who performs, dances, and plays music.
III. It was mentioned by Kashmiri Sufi Saint, Sheikh Noor-ud-din Noorani (RA) in his verses and travel book of English writer, Sir Walter Lawrence.
column14: Bhand Pather is the traditional Kashmiri folk theatre where a single performer (Bhand) acts, dances, and plays music. It was mentioned by Sheikh Noor-ud-din Noorani and Sir Walter Lawrence in "The Valley of Kashmir."

column6:
Which of the following statements about Mughal Gardens in Kashmir are correct?
I. Nishant Bagh laid out in the 17th century, is located directly along the eastern bank of the Dal Lake.
II. The two most important structures within the Shalimar Bagh are the Pink Pavilion, in the Diwan-i-Aam zone of the garden, and the Black Pavilion, located in the Diwan-i-Khas.
III. Achabal Bagh was also known as Sahebabad during the Mughal period, in memory of the Mughal Emperor Jahangir.
column14: I and II are correct. Nishant Bagh (1632) is on the eastern bank of Dal Lake. Shalimar Bagh has Pink Pavilion (Diwan-i-Aam) and Black Pavilion (Diwan-i-Khas). Achabal Bagh was known as Sahebabad in memory of Empress Noor Jahan, not Jahangir. So III is incorrect.

column6:
Which of the following statements about the geographic characteristics of the Jammu region are correct?
I. Jammu city is situated on a series of uneven ridges of low heights in the Shivalik Hills.
II. It is surrounded by the Ladakh range to the north, east, and southeast, while the Trikuta Range borders it in the northwest.
column14: Both statements are correct. Jammu city is in the Shivalik Hills on uneven ridges. It is surrounded by Ladakh range (north, east, southeast) and Trikuta Range (northwest).

column6: Dachigam National Park is located in which mountain range?
column14: Dachigam National Park, famous for the Hangul deer, is located in the Zabarwan Range near Srinagar in Kashmir.

column6: A Census planned in J & K in early 2026 is aimed at conservation of which species?
column14: The 2026 census in J&K is specifically aimed at the conservation of the Hangul (Kashmir Stag), which is the state animal of Jammu and Kashmir and an endangered species found in Dachigam National Park.

column6:
Which of the following rivers are tributaries of the river Chenab?
I. Ujh river,
II. Tawi river,
III. Poonch river,
IV. Neeru river.
column14: Tawi, Poonch, and Neeru are tributaries of Chenab. Ujh river is a tributary of Ravi, not Chenab. So II, III, and IV are correct.

column6: The J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019 came into effect on:
column14: The J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019 came into effect on October 31, 2019, when the erstwhile state was bifurcated into two UTs: Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh.

column6: Which of the following is NOT a tourist destination in Jammu and Kashmir UT?
column14: Kanyakumari is located in Tamil Nadu at the southernmost tip of India. Patnitop, Gulmarg, and Pahalgam are all famous tourist destinations in Jammu and Kashmir.

column6: The Wular Lake in J&K is associated with which river?
column14: Wular Lake, one of the largest freshwater lakes in Asia, is located on the Jhelum River in Bandipora district of Kashmir. It acts as a natural reservoir for the Jhelum.

column6: Which of the following crops is NOT primarily grown in the Jammu region?
column14: Saffron is primarily grown in the Kashmir region (Pampore area), not in the Jammu region. Rice, wheat, and maize are all major crops of the Jammu region.

column6: The famous Vaishno Devi shrine is located in which hill range?
column14: The Vaishno Devi shrine is located in the Trikuta Hills at an altitude of about 5200 feet, near Katra in the Reasi district of Jammu division.

column6:
Which of the following statements about the Census of India is correct?
I. The first Census in India was conducted in 1872.
II. Census is conducted every 5 years in India.
III. The Census provides data on population, demography, and socio-economic characteristics.
column14: I and III are correct. The first Census was in 1872 under Lord Mayo. Census is conducted every 10 years, not 5 years. It provides comprehensive demographic and socio-economic data.

column6: The ozone layer is found in which part of the atmosphere?
column14: The ozone layer is located in the stratosphere, approximately 10-50 km above Earth's surface. It absorbs harmful UV radiation from the sun.

column6: Which of the following is a conventional source of energy?
column14: Coal is a conventional (non-renewable) source of energy. Solar, wind, and biomass are non-conventional (renewable) sources of energy.

column6: The Greenhouse Effect is primarily caused by:
column14: Carbon dioxide (CO2) is the primary greenhouse gas responsible for the greenhouse effect. Other greenhouse gases include methane, nitrous oxide, and water vapor.

column6: Which river is known as the "Sorrow of Bengal"?
column14: Damodar River is called the "Sorrow of Bengal" due to its frequent flooding. After the construction of dams, it is now called the "River of Joy." Kosi is known as the "Sorrow of Bihar."

column6:
Consider the following statements about the Accounting Equation:
I. The accounting equation is always: Assets = Liabilities + Capital.
II. Every transaction affects at least two elements of the accounting equation.
III. The accounting equation must remain balanced after every transaction.

Which of the above statements are correct?
column14: All three statements are correct. The fundamental accounting equation is Assets = Liabilities + Capital. Every transaction has dual effect, and the equation always remains balanced.

column6:
Match the following: Book of Original Entry
1. Journal,
2. Cash Book,
3. Purchase Book,
4. Sales Book. Primary Purpose i. Record all cash transactions, ii. Record credit purchases, iii. Record chronological transactions, iv. Record credit sales.
column14: Journal records chronological transactions (iii). Cash Book records all cash transactions (i). Purchase Book records credit purchases (ii). Sales Book records credit sales (iv). So 1-iii, 2-i, 3-ii, 4-iv is correct.

column5: Elements of Double Entry Book Keeping
column6:
Which of the following statements about Double Entry Book Keeping are correct?
I. Every debit has a corresponding credit.
II. The total of all debits must equal the total of all credits.
III. Personal accounts are debited when the receiver receives something.
column14: All three statements are correct. Double entry system follows the rule that every debit has an equal credit. Personal account rule: Debit the receiver, Credit the giver.

column6:
Consider the following statements about Trial Balance:
I. Trial Balance is a statement of all ledger account balances.
II. It proves the arithmetical accuracy of bookkeeping.
III. A tallied trial balance guarantees absence of all errors.

Which of the above statements are correct?
column14: I and II are correct. A tallied trial balance does not guarantee absence of all errors (errors of omission, commission, principle, and compensating errors may still exist). So III is incorrect.

column6:
Match the following: Type of Account
1. Real Account,
2. Personal Account,
3. Nominal Account. Rule i. Debit the receiver, Credit the giver, ii. Debit what comes in, Credit what goes out, iii. Debit all expenses and losses, Credit all incomes and gains.
column14: Real Account rule: Debit what comes in, Credit what goes out (ii). Personal Account rule: Debit the receiver, Credit the giver (i). Nominal Account rule: Debit all expenses and losses, Credit all incomes and gains (iii). So 1-ii, 2-i, 3-iii is correct.

column6:
Which of the following statements about Cash Book are correct?
I. Cash Book serves as both a journal and a ledger.
II. A double column cash book records cash and bank transactions.
III. Petty Cash Book is maintained for small expenses under imprest system.
column14: All three statements are correct. Cash Book is both a book of original entry and a ledger. Double column cash book has cash and bank columns. Petty Cash Book uses the imprest system for small payments.

column6:
Consider the following statements about Bank Reconciliation Statement:
I. It reconciles the difference between Cash Book balance and Pass Book balance.
II. Direct deposits by customers increase the pass book balance but not the cash book.
III. Bank charges decrease the cash book balance but not the pass book.

Which of the above statements are correct?
column14: I and II are correct. Bank charges decrease the pass book balance first, and then are recorded in cash book. So III is incorrect (it decreases pass book first, not cash book).

column6: Which of the following is NOT a financial statement?
column14: Bank Reconciliation Statement is not a financial statement. It is a statement prepared to reconcile differences between cash book and pass book. Trading Account, Profit and Loss Account, and Balance Sheet are the main financial statements.

column6:
Match the following: Financial
Statement
1. Trading Account,
2. Profit and Loss Account,
3. Balance Sheet,
4. Cash Flow Statement. Purpose i. Ascertain net profit or loss, ii. Show financial position, iii. Ascertain gross profit or loss, iv. Show cash movements.
column14: Trading Account ascertains gross profit/loss (iii). Profit and Loss Account ascertains net profit/loss (i). Balance Sheet shows financial position (ii). Cash Flow Statement shows cash movements (iv). So 1-iii, 2-i, 3-ii, 4-iv is correct.

column5: Elements of Double Entry Book Keeping
column6:
Which of the following statements about Depreciation are correct?
I. Depreciation is a non-cash expense.
II. Straight Line Method charges equal depreciation every year.
III. Written Down Value Method charges higher depreciation in initial years.
column14: All three statements are correct. Depreciation is a non-cash expense that allocates the cost of an asset over its useful life. SLM charges equal amount. WDV charges higher in initial years.

column6: Which of the following is an intangible asset?
column14: Goodwill is an intangible asset as it cannot be seen or touched but has value. Machinery, stock, and furniture are tangible assets.

column6:
Match the following: Ratio
1. Current Ratio,
2. Quick Ratio,
3. Stock Turnover Ratio,
4. Debt-Equity Ratio. Formula i. Cost of Goods Sold / Average Stock, ii. Current Assets / Current Liabilities, iii. (Current Assets - Stock) / Current Liabilities, iv. Long-term Debt / Shareholders' Funds.
column14: Current Ratio = Current Assets / Current Liabilities (ii). Quick Ratio = (Current Assets - Stock) / Current Liabilities (iii). Stock Turnover Ratio = COGS / Average Stock (i). Debt-Equity Ratio = Long-term Debt / Shareholders' Funds (iv). So 1-ii, 2-iii, 3-i, 4-iv is correct.

column6:
Which of the following statements about Cost Accounting are correct?
I. Cost accounting helps in cost control and cost reduction.
II. Budgetary control involves preparation and comparison of budgets.
III. Standard costing sets predetermined costs for comparison.
column14: All three statements are correct. Cost accounting provides data for cost control. Budgetary control compares actual with budgets. Standard costing uses predetermined standards.

column6:
Consider the following statements about PFMS:
I. PFMS stands for Public Financial Management System.
II. It is used for tracking government expenditure in real-time.
III. It helps in direct benefit transfer to beneficiaries.

Which of the above statements are correct?
column14: All three statements are correct. PFMS is the Public Financial Management System used by the Government of India for real-time tracking of expenditure and direct benefit transfers.

column6: Which of the following is a direct tax?
column14: Income Tax is a direct tax as it is levied directly on the income of individuals and companies. GST, Customs Duty, and Excise Duty are indirect taxes.

column6:
Match the following: Tax Type
1. Direct Tax,
2. Indirect Tax,
3. Progressive Tax,
4. Proportional Tax. Example i. Sales Tax, ii. Wealth Tax, iii. Income Tax, iv. GST.
column14:
1 -> ii (Direct Tax -> Wealth Tax)
2 -> i (Indirect Tax -> Sales Tax)
3 -> iii (Progressive Tax -> Income Tax)
4 -> iv (Proportional Tax -> GST)

column6:
Which of the following statements about Voucher Approach are correct?
I. Voucher system ensures proper authorization of payments.
II. It helps in internal control over cash disbursements.
III. Vouchers are prepared for every payment transaction.
column14: All three statements are correct. The voucher system ensures authorization, provides internal control, and requires vouchers for all payments.

column6:
Consider the following statements about Social Accounting:
I. It measures social costs and benefits of business activities.
II. Social audit assesses the social impact of an organization.
III. It is mandatory for all companies in India.

Which of the above statements are correct?
column14: I and II are correct. Social accounting measures social impact and social audit assesses it. However, it is not mandatory for all companies in India (only certain categories under CSR rules). So III is incorrect.

column6:
Which of the following statements about Cash-Based Accounting are correct?
I. Revenue is recognized when cash is received.
II. Expenses are recorded when cash is paid.
III. It is simpler than accrual basis accounting.
column14: All three statements are correct. In cash-based accounting, revenue and expenses are recognized when cash is received or paid. It is simpler than accrual basis but less accurate for matching revenues with expenses.

column6:
Match the following: Accounting Concept
1. Going Concern,
2. Business Entity,
3. Money Measurement,
4. Dual Aspect. Meaning i. Business is separate from its owner, ii. Assume business will continue indefinitely, iii. Record only measurable transactions, iv. Every transaction has two effects.
column14: Going Concern assumes business continues indefinitely (ii). Business Entity means business is separate from owner (i). Money Measurement records only measurable transactions (iii). Dual Aspect means every transaction has two effects (iv). So 1-ii, 2-i, 3-iii, 4-iv is correct.

column6: Which of the following is NOT a method of calculating depreciation?
column14: First In First Out (FIFO) is a method of inventory valuation, not depreciation. Straight Line Method, Written Down Value Method, and Annuity Method are all methods of calculating depreciation.

column6:
Consider the following statements about Working Capital:
I. Working Capital = Current Assets - Current Liabilities.
II. Positive working capital indicates good short-term financial health.
III. Working capital turnover ratio measures efficiency of working capital usage.

Which of the above statements are correct?
column14: All three statements are correct. Working capital is the difference between current assets and current liabilities. Positive working capital is generally good. Working capital turnover ratio measures how efficiently working capital is used.

column6:
Which of the following statements about Financial Management are correct?
I. It aims at wealth maximization of shareholders.
II. It involves decisions about investment, financing, and dividends.
III. Financial management is concerned with only long-term decisions.
column14: I and II are correct. Financial management aims at wealth maximization and involves investment, financing, and dividend decisions. It is concerned with both short-term and long-term decisions, not only long-term. So III is incorrect.

column6:
Match the following: Financial Statement Analysis Tool
1. Comparative Statements,
2. Common Size Statements,
3. Trend Analysis,
4. Ratio Analysis. Purpose i. Show percentage relationship, ii. Show trends over years, iii. Compare with industry standards, iv. Compare year-to-year changes.
column14: Comparative Statements compare year-to-year changes (iv). Common Size Statements show percentage relationship (i). Trend Analysis shows trends over years (ii). Ratio Analysis compares with industry standards (iii). So 1-iv, 2-i, 3-ii, 4-iii is correct.

column6:
Which of the following statements about Ledger Accounts are correct?
I. Ledger is the principal book of accounts.
II. Posting is the process of transferring entries from journal to ledger.
III. Balancing of ledger accounts is done to find the net position.
column14: All three statements are correct. Ledger is the principal book where all accounts are maintained. Posting transfers entries from journal to ledger. Balancing finds the net position (debit or credit balance).

column6: Which of the following is a capital receipt?
column14: Sale of old machinery is a capital receipt as it results from sale of a capital asset. Sale of goods, commission, and rent are revenue receipts.

column6:
Match the following: Indian Accounting Standard
1. Ind AS 1,
2. Ind AS 2,
3. Ind AS 7,
4. Ind AS 115. Related To i. Presentation of Financial Statements, ii. Revenue from Contracts with Customers, iii. Statement of Cash Flows, iv. Inventories.
column14: Ind AS 1: Presentation of Financial Statements (i). Ind AS 2: Inventories (iv). Ind AS 7: Statement of Cash Flows (iii). Ind AS 115: Revenue from Contracts with Customers (ii). So 1-i, 2-iv, 3-iii, 4-ii is correct.

column6:
Which of the following statements about Audit are correct?
I. Internal audit is conducted by employees of the organization.
II. External audit is conducted by independent auditors.
III. Statutory audit is mandatory under the Companies Act.
column14: All three statements are correct. Internal audit is done by employees, external audit by independent auditors, and statutory audit is mandatory for companies under the Companies Act, 2013.

column6: Choose the option that correctly punctuates the sentence: "The proposal which was submitted last week however requires further revision"
column7: The proposal, which was submitted last week however, requires further revision.
column8: The proposal which was submitted last week, however, requires further revision.
column9: The proposal, which was submitted last week, however requires further revision.
column10: The proposal, which was submitted last week, however, requires further revision.
column14: The correct punctuation is: "The proposal, which was submitted last week, however, requires further revision." The non-restrictive clause "which was submitted last week" needs commas, and "however" as a conjunctive adverb needs commas around it.

column6: Identify the type of clause in the sentence below: "What the committee decided surprised everyone present." The clause "What the committee decided" is a:
column7: Noun clause functioning as the subject
column10: Independent clause with an implied subject
column14: "What the committee decided" is a noun clause functioning as the subject of the sentence. It acts as a noun (the subject) and is introduced by the relative pronoun "what."

column6: In which sentence is the word "bank" used as a homonym when compared to its use in "She deposited the cheque at the bank"?
column7: The pilot had to bank the aircraft sharply during the landing.
column8: The children played on the bank of the river after school.
column9: The bank approved the loan after a detailed review.
column10: He works at a multinational bank in the city.
column14: In the original sentence, "bank" means a financial institution. In option A, "bank" means to tilt or turn (verb), which is a different meaning but same spelling - making it a homonym. Option B uses "bank" as river bank (noun), also a homonym, but A is the best answer as it shows a completely different grammatical function (verb vs noun).

column6: Choose the sentence in which the correct homophone has been used:
column7: The principal asked the students to bare the consequences of their actions.
column8: She decided to compliment the dress with a matching scarf.
column9: The hikers were advised to pause the trail before nightfall.
column10: He could not cite a single example to support his claim.
column14: "Cite" (to quote as evidence) is correctly used in D. In A, it should be "bear" not "bare." In B, it should be "complement" not "compliment." In C, "advised" is correct but "pause" should be "paws" or the sentence is awkward. D is clearly correct with "cite."

column6: Choose the sentence in which the pronoun usage is grammatically correct:
column7: Each of the participants must submit their assignment by Friday.
column8: Neither of the proposals achieved their intended objective.
column9: Every applicant should bring his or her identification for verification.
column10: The committee reached their decision after prolonged deliberation.
column14: "Every applicant should bring his or her identification" is grammatically correct. "Each" and "Neither" require singular pronouns (his/her, not their). "Committee" as a singular entity takes "its" not "their" in formal grammar.

column6: Identify the sentence with a clear and unambiguous pronoun reference:
column7: When Sara met Lina, she was already upset.
column8: The students informed the teacher that they would submit the project late.
column9: Rahul told Amit that he had won the scholarship.
column10: After the report was revised, it was criticized by the editor.
column14: In D, "it" clearly refers to "the report." In A, "she" is ambiguous (Sara or Lina?). In B, "they" could refer to students or teacher. In C, "he" is ambiguous (Rahul or Amit?).

column6: Choose the option that correctly converts the following sentence into indirect speech: The professor said, "I will review your thesis tomorrow."
column7: The professor said that he would review your thesis tomorrow.
column8: The professor said that he will review your thesis the next day.
column9: The professor said that he would review my thesis the next day.
column10: The professor said that I would review your thesis the next day.
column14: In indirect speech: "I" becomes "he," "your" becomes "my," "will" becomes "would," and "tomorrow" becomes "the next day." So: "The professor said that he would review my thesis the next day."

column6:
Rearrange the following sentences to form a meaningful paragraph:
I. He worked hard to achieve his goals.
II. Success did not come easily to him.
III. Eventually, his efforts paid off.
IV. From a young age, he was determined to succeed.
column14: The logical sequence is: IV (determination from young age) → II (success didn't come easily) → I (worked hard) → III (efforts paid off). This shows the progression from determination through struggle to success.

column6: The idiom "too little, too late" most precisely conveys that the apology:
column8: Failed to address the full extent of the controversy
column9: Was inadequate in both substance and timing to be effective
column10: Was overshadowed by more pressing political developments
column14: "Too little, too late" means something is insufficient in amount (substance) and also delayed (timing), making it ineffective. It emphasizes both inadequacy and tardiness.

column6: Which word is the most appropriate synonym of "prolix" in the context: "The editor criticized the article for its prolix treatment of an otherwise simple topic"?
column14: "Prolix" means using too many words, wordy. "Verbose" is the closest synonym meaning excessively wordy. "Discursive" means digressing, "redundant" means repetitive, "diffuse" means spread out.

column5: Methods of Collecting Primary and Secondary Data
column6:
Consider the following statements about data collection:
I. Primary data is collected directly from the source for the first time.
II. Secondary data has already been collected and published by someone else.
III. Questionnaire method is a technique of collecting primary data.

Which of the above statements are correct?
column14: All three statements are correct. Primary data is original data collected firsthand. Secondary data is already published. Questionnaire is a primary data collection method.

column6:
Match the following: Measure of Central Tendency
1. Mean,
2. Median,
3. Mode,
4. Geometric Mean. Characteristic i. Most frequently occurring value, ii. Affected by extreme values, iii. Middle value when arranged in order, iv. Useful for calculating average rates.
column14: Mean is affected by extreme values (ii). Median is the middle value (iii). Mode is most frequently occurring (i). Geometric Mean is useful for average rates (iv). So 1-ii, 2-iii, 3-i, 4-iv is correct.

column6:
Which of the following statements about Probability are correct?
I. Probability ranges from 0 to
1.
II. The sum of probabilities of all possible outcomes is
1.
III. Probability of a sure event is 0.
column14:
I and II are correct. Probability of a sure event is 1, not
0. Probability of an impossible event is
0. So III is incorrect.

column6:
Consider the following statements about Index Numbers:
I. Wholesale Price Index (WPI) measures changes in wholesale prices.
II. Consumer Price Index (CPI) measures changes in retail prices.
III. Index numbers are specialized averages used to measure relative changes.

Which of the above statements are correct?
column14: All three statements are correct. WPI measures wholesale price changes, CPI measures retail price changes (consumer prices), and index numbers are indeed specialized averages for measuring relative changes over time.

column6: Which of the following is NOT a test of a good index number?
column14: Mean Test is not a standard test for index numbers. The standard tests are: Unit Test, Time Reversal Test, Factor Reversal Test, and Circular Test. Mean Test is not recognized.

column6:
Match the following: Demographic Measure
1. Crude Birth Rate,
2. Crude Death Rate,
3. Gross Reproduction Rate,
4. Net Reproduction Rate. Formula i. (Number of deaths / Mid-year population) × 1000, ii. (Number of live births / Mid-year population) × 1000, iii. Average number of daughters born to a woman, iv. GRR adjusted for mortality.
column14: CBR = (Live births / Mid-year population) × 1000 (ii). CDR = (Deaths / Mid-year population) × 1000 (i). GRR = Average daughters per woman (iii). NRR = GRR adjusted for mortality (iv). So 1-ii, 2-i, 3-iii, 4-iv is correct.

column6:
Which of the following statements about Vital Statistics are correct?
I. Vital statistics relate to births, deaths, marriages, and divorces.
II. They are used for planning health and family welfare programs.
III. The Census of India collects vital statistics through sample registration system.
column14: All three statements are correct. Vital statistics include births, deaths, marriages, and divorces. They are used for health and welfare planning. In India, the Sample Registration System (SRS) collects vital statistics between censuses.

column6:
Consider the following statements about Tabulation:
I. Tabulation is the systematic arrangement of data in rows and columns.
II. It simplifies complex data for easy understanding.
III. A table should have a clear title and footnotes if necessary.

Which of the above statements are correct?
column14: All three statements are correct. Tabulation arranges data systematically in rows and columns, simplifies complex data, and requires clear title, headings, and footnotes for completeness.

column5: Measures of Central Tendency and Dispersion
column6: Which of the following is a measure of dispersion?
column14: Standard Deviation is a measure of dispersion (spread of data). Mean, Median, and Mode are measures of central tendency (central values).

column6:
Match the following: Statistical Concept
1. Primary Data,
2. Secondary Data,
3. Qualitative Data,
4. Quantitative Data. Description i. Data collected from published sources, ii. First-hand information, iii. Non-numerical characteristics, iv. Numerical information.
column14:
1 -> ii (Primary Data -> First-hand information)
Explanation: Fresh data collected directly by the researcher.
2 -> i (Secondary Data -> Data collected from published sources)
Explanation: Pre-existing data gathered by someone else.
3 -> iii (Qualitative Data -> Non-numerical characteristics)
Explanation: Descriptive attributes that do not use numbers.
4 -> iv (Quantitative Data -> Numerical information)
Explanation: Measurable data expressed as numbers.

column6:
Consider the following statements about the number 45678x9231:
I. If x = 0, the number is divisible by
3.
II. If x = 3, the number is divisible by
3.
III. If x = 6, the number is divisible by
3.
IV. If x = 9, the number is divisible by
3.

How many of the above statements are correct?
column14:
Sum of digits = 4+5+6+7+8+x+9+2+3+1 = 45+x. For divisibility by 3, (45+x) must be divisible by
3. Since 45 is divisible by 3, x must be divisible by
3. So x = 0, 3, 6, 9 all work. All four statements are correct.

column6:
If x = 2¹⁰ × 5⁶,

which of the following statements are correct?
I. The number ends with 6 zeros.
II. The number is divisible by 10⁶.
III. The number is a perfect square.
column14: x = 2¹⁰ × 5⁶ = 2⁴ × (2×5)⁶ = 16 × 10⁶ = 16,000,000. It ends with 6 zeros (I correct). It is divisible by 10⁶ (II correct). III. The number is a perfect square (Correct): A number is a perfect square if all the exponents in its prime factorization are even numbers. So all three are correct. Answer is D.

column5: Simple Compound Interest and Permutations Combinations
column6:
Match the following: Mathematical Concept
1. Simple Interest,
2. Compound Interest,
3. Permutation,
4. Combination. Application i. A = P(1 + r/n)^(nt), ii. A = P(1 + rt), iii. n! / (n-r)!, iv. n! / [r!(n-r)!].
column14: Simple Interest: A = P(1 + rt) (ii). Compound Interest: A = P(1 + r/n)^(nt) (i). Permutation: n!/(n-r)! (iii). Combination: n!/[r!(n-r)!] (iv). So 1-ii, 2-i, 3-iii, 4-iv is correct.

column6:
Consider the following statements about linear equations:
I. A linear equation in two variables has infinitely many solutions.
II. The graph of a linear equation in two variables is a straight line.
III. Two linear equations in two variables always have a unique solution.

Which of the above statements are correct?
column14: I and II are correct. A single linear equation in two variables has infinitely many solutions. Its graph is a straight line. However, two linear equations may have unique solution, no solution, or infinitely many solutions (if parallel or coincident). So III is incorrect.

column6:
Which of the following statements about Set Theory are correct?
I. The union of two sets contains all elements from both sets.
II. The intersection of two sets contains only common elements.
III. The complement of a set contains all elements not in the set.
column14: All three statements are correct. Union (A∪B) contains all elements from A or B. Intersection (A∩B) contains only common elements. Complement (A') contains all elements in universal set not in A.

column6:
Match the following: Matrix Operation
1. Addition of matrices,
2. Multiplication of matrices,
3. Determinant,
4. Inverse. Result i. Possible only if order is same, ii. Possible if columns of first = rows of second, iii. Defined only for square matrices, iv. Exists only if determinant is non-zero.
column14: Matrix addition requires same order (i). Multiplication requires columns of first = rows of second (ii). Determinant is defined only for square matrices (iii). Inverse exists only if determinant is non-zero (iv). So 1-i, 2-ii, 3-iii, 4-iv is correct.

column6:
Consider the following statements about Probability:
I. P(A∪B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A∩B).
II. For independent events, P(A∩B) = P(A) × P(B).
III. The sum of probabilities of all outcomes in a sample space is
1.

Which of the above statements are correct?
column14: All three statements are correct. I is the addition theorem of probability. II is the multiplication theorem for independent events. III is the axiom of probability that total probability equals 1.

column6:
Which of the following statements about Coordinate Geometry are correct?
I. The distance between two points (x₁,y₁) and (x₂,y₂) is √[(x₂-x₁)² + (y₂-y₁)²].
II. The midpoint of a line segment joining (x₁,y₁) and (x₂,y₂) is [(x₁+x₂)/2, (y₁+y₂)/2].
III. The slope of a line passing through (x₁,y₁) and (x₂,y₂) is (y₂-y₁)/(x₂-x₁).
column14: All three statements are correct. I is the distance formula. II is the midpoint formula. III is the slope formula. All are standard formulas in coordinate geometry.

column6: Match the following: Limit/Derivative 1. lim(x→0) sin(x)/x, 2. lim(x→0) (1-cos(x))/x, 3. d/dx(xⁿ), 4. d/dx(eˣ). Result i. 0, ii. 1, iii. nxⁿ⁻¹, iv. eˣ.
column14: lim(x→0) sin(x)/x = 1 (ii). lim(x→0) (1-cos(x))/x = 0 (i). d/dx(xⁿ) = nxⁿ⁻¹ (iii). d/dx(eˣ) = eˣ (iv). So 1-ii, 2-i, 3-iii, 4-iv is correct.

column6:
Consider the following statements about Vectors:
I. Two vectors are equal if they have the same magnitude and direction.
II. The dot product of two perpendicular vectors is zero.
III. The cross product of two vectors results in a scalar quantity.

Which of the above statements are correct?
column14: I and II are correct. Equal vectors have same magnitude and direction. Dot product of perpendicular vectors is zero. Cross product results in a vector (not scalar) quantity. So III is incorrect.

column6:
Consider the following statements about Economics:
I. Economics is the study of how society manages its scarce resources.
II. Microeconomics deals with individual economic units.
III. Macroeconomics deals with the economy as a whole.

Which of the above statements are correct?
column14: All three statements are correct. Economics studies scarcity and choice. Microeconomics focuses on individuals, firms, and markets. Macroeconomics focuses on aggregate variables like GDP, inflation, and unemployment.

column6:
Match the following: Economic Concept
1. Demand,
2. Supply,
3. Equilibrium,
4. Elasticity. Description i. Desire backed by ability and willingness to pay, ii. Amount of a good sellers are willing to sell, iii. Quantity demanded equals quantity supplied, iv. Responsiveness of quantity to price changes.
column14: Demand is desire backed by ability and willingness (i). Supply is amount sellers are willing to sell (ii). Equilibrium is where demand equals supply (iii). Elasticity is responsiveness to price changes (iv). So 1-i, 2-ii, 3-iii, 4-iv is correct.

column6:
Which of the following statements about Fiscal Policy are correct?
I. Fiscal policy involves government spending and taxation.
II. Expansionary fiscal policy increases aggregate demand.
III. Contractionary fiscal policy is used to control inflation.
column14: All three statements are correct. Fiscal policy uses government spending and taxation. Expansionary policy (increased spending, decreased taxes) boosts aggregate demand. Contractionary policy (decreased spending, increased taxes) controls inflation.

column6:
Consider the following statements about Monetary Policy:
I. It is formulated by the Reserve Bank of India.
II. Repo rate is the rate at which RBI lends to commercial banks.
III. Reverse repo rate is the rate at which RBI borrows from commercial banks.

Which of the above statements are correct?
column14: All three statements are correct. RBI formulates monetary policy. Repo rate is the rate at which RBI lends to banks. Reverse repo rate is the rate at which RBI borrows from banks.

column6: Which of the following is NOT a factor of production?
column14: Money is not a factor of production. The four factors of production are Land, Labour, Capital (not money), and Entrepreneurship. Money is a medium of exchange, not a productive resource itself.

column5: Pricing under Various Forms of Market
column6:
Match the following: Market Structure
1. Perfect Competition,
2. Monopoly,
3. Oligopoly,
4. Monopolistic Competition. Characteristic i. Single seller, ii. Many sellers with differentiated products, iii. Few large sellers, iv. Many sellers with identical products.
column14: Perfect Competition: many sellers, identical products (iv). Monopoly: single seller (i). Oligopoly: few large sellers (iii). Monopolistic Competition: many sellers, differentiated products (ii). So 1-iv, 2-i, 3-iii, 4-ii is correct.

column5: Concept and Measurement of National Income
column6:
Which of the following statements about National Income are correct?
I. GDP is the total value of goods and services produced within the country.
II. GNP = GDP + Net factor income from abroad.
III. National Income is calculated at factor cost.
column14: All three statements are correct. GDP measures domestic production. GNP includes net factor income from abroad. National Income (NNP at factor cost) is calculated at factor cost.

column6:
Consider the following statements about Economic Planning in India:
I. The Planning Commission was established in 1950.
II. NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission in 2015.
III. The First Five Year Plan focused on agriculture.

Which of the above statements are correct?
column14: All three statements are correct. Planning Commission was established in 1950. NITI Aayog replaced it on January 1, 2015. The First Five Year Plan (1951-56) focused on agriculture and irrigation.

column6:
Which of the following statements about the Role of RBI are correct?
I. RBI is the central bank of India.
II. It acts as banker to the government.
III. It regulates the banking sector in India.
column14: All three statements are correct. RBI is India's central bank established in 1935. It acts as banker to the central and state governments. It regulates and supervises the banking sector through various mechanisms.

column6:
Match the following: Economic Reform
1. Liberalization,
2. Privatization,
3. Globalization,
4. GST Implementation. Year/Description i. 1991, ii. Disinvestment of PSUs, iii. Integration with world economy, iv. 2017.
column14: Liberalization started in 1991 (i). Privatization involves disinvestment of PSUs (ii). Globalization means integration with world economy (iii). GST was implemented in 2017 (iv). So 1-i, 2-ii, 3-iii, 4-iv is correct.

column6:
Consider the following statements about Newton's Laws:
I. First law defines inertia.
II. Second law states F = ma.
III. Third law states action and reaction are equal and opposite.

Which of the above statements are correct?
column14: All three statements are correct. First law is the law of inertia. Second law is F = ma. Third law states that every action has an equal and opposite reaction.

column6:
Match the following: Physical Quantity
1. Electric Current,
2. Voltage,
3. Power,
4. Energy. Unit i. Volt, ii. Ampere, iii. Watt, iv. Joule.
column14: Electric Current is measured in Ampere (ii). Voltage is measured in Volt (i). Power is measured in Watt (iii). Energy is measured in Joule (iv). So 1-ii, 2-i, 3-iii, 4-iv is correct.

column6:
Which of the following statements about Chemical Equations are correct?
I. A balanced chemical equation has equal atoms on both sides.
II. Chemical equations represent the law of conservation of mass.
III. The arrow in a chemical equation means "reacts to form."
column14: All three statements are correct. A balanced equation has equal atoms on both sides. It represents conservation of mass. The arrow (→) means "reacts to form" or "yields."

column6:
Consider the following statements about Metals and Non-metals:
I. Metals are generally good conductors of heat and electricity.
II. Non-metals are generally brittle and dull.
III. Metals form basic oxides while non-metals form acidic oxides.

Which of the above statements are correct?
column14: All three statements are correct. Metals are good conductors, non-metals are brittle and dull (except graphite), and their oxides are basic (metals) or acidic (non-metals).

column6: Which of the following is a non-conventional source of energy?
column14: Solar energy is a non-conventional (renewable) source of energy. Coal, petroleum, and natural gas are conventional (non-renewable, fossil fuel) sources.

column6:
Match the following: Nutrient
1. Vitamin A,
2. Vitamin C,
3. Vitamin D,
4. Vitamin B1. Deficiency Disease i. Scurvy, ii. Rickets, iii. Night blindness, iv. Beriberi.
column14: Vitamin A deficiency causes Night blindness (iii). Vitamin C deficiency causes Scurvy (i). Vitamin D deficiency causes Rickets (ii). Vitamin B1 (Thiamine) deficiency causes Beriberi (iv). So 1-iii, 2-i, 3-ii, 4-iv is correct.

column6:
Which of the following statements about the Ecosystem are correct?
I. Producers form the base of the food chain.
II. Consumers depend on producers for food.
III. Decomposers break down dead organic matter.
column14: All three statements are correct. Producers (plants) form the base by converting sunlight to energy. Consumers (herbivores, carnivores) depend on producers. Decomposers (bacteria, fungi) break down dead matter and recycle nutrients.

column6:
Consider the following statements about Environmental Pollution:
I. Greenhouse effect leads to global warming.
II. Ozone depletion is caused by CFCs.
III. Acid rain is caused by oxides of sulfur and nitrogen.
column14: All three statements are correct. Greenhouse gases trap heat causing global warming. Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) deplete the ozone layer. Oxides of sulfur (SOx) and nitrogen (NOx) cause acid rain.

column6: Which of the following is a communicable disease?
column14: Tuberculosis is a communicable (infectious) disease caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Diabetes, cancer, and hypertension are non-communicable diseases.

column6:
Match the following: Process in Plants
1. Photosynthesis,
2. Respiration,
3. Transpiration,
4. Conduction. Description i. Breakdown of glucose to release energy, ii. Transport of water and minerals, iii. Loss of water vapor through stomata, iv. Conversion of light energy to chemical energy.
column14: Photosynthesis converts light energy to chemical energy (iv). Respiration breaks down glucose to release energy (i). Transpiration is loss of water vapor through stomata (iii). Conduction is transport of water and minerals (ii). So 1-iv, 2-i, 3-iii, 4-ii is correct.

column6:
Which of the following statements about Computer Fundamentals are correct?
I. CPU is the brain of the computer.
II. RAM is volatile memory.
III. ROM is non-volatile memory.
column14: All three statements are correct. CPU (Central Processing Unit) is the brain. RAM (Random Access Memory) is volatile (loses data when power off). ROM (Read Only Memory) is non-volatile (retains data without power).

column6:
Match the following: Component
1. ALU,
2. CU,
3. RAM,
4. Hard Disk. Function i. Stores data temporarily, ii. Performs arithmetic and logical operations, iii. Controls and coordinates operations, iv. Permanent storage.
column14: ALU performs arithmetic and logical operations (ii). CU controls and coordinates operations (iii). RAM stores data temporarily (i). Hard Disk provides permanent storage (iv). So 1-ii, 2-iii, 3-i, 4-iv is correct.

column6:
Which of the following statements about Operating Systems are correct?
I. Operating system manages computer hardware and software resources.
II. Windows, Linux, and macOS are examples of operating systems.
III. Operating system acts as an interface between user and computer.
column14: All three statements are correct. OS manages resources, provides examples (Windows, Linux, macOS), and acts as an interface between user and hardware.

column5: MS Word MS Excel MS PowerPoint
column6:
Consider the following statements about MS Office:
I. MS Word is used for word processing.
II. MS Excel is used for spreadsheet calculations.
III. MS PowerPoint is used for creating presentations.

Which of the above statements are correct?
column14: All three statements are correct. MS Word is for word processing, MS Excel for spreadsheets and calculations, MS PowerPoint for presentations.

column6: Which of the following is an input device?
column14: Keyboard is an input device used to enter data into the computer. Monitor, printer, and speaker are output devices that display or produce output.

column6:
Match the following: Computer Term
1. Hardware,
2. Software,
3. Firmware,
4. Malware. Description i. Physical components of computer, ii. Programs and applications, iii. Software embedded in hardware, iv. Malicious software.
column14: Hardware is physical components (i). Software is programs and applications (ii). Firmware is software embedded in hardware (iii). Malware is malicious software (iv). So 1-i, 2-ii, 3-iii, 4-iv is correct.

column6:
Which of the following statements about Computer Networks are correct?
I. LAN covers a small geographical area.
II. WAN covers a large geographical area.
III. Internet is a network of networks.
column14: All three statements are correct. LAN (Local Area Network) covers small areas like offices. WAN (Wide Area Network) covers large areas like countries. Internet is indeed a global network of interconnected networks.

column6:
Consider the following statements about Internet and Email:
I. HTTP is used for transferring web pages.
II. SMTP is used for sending emails.
III. POP3 is used for receiving emails.

Which of the above statements are correct?
column14: All three statements are correct. HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol) transfers web pages. SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) sends emails. POP3 (Post Office Protocol 3) receives emails from server to local computer.

column6: Which of the following is an example of system software?
column14: Operating System is system software that manages computer hardware and software resources. MS Word, Google Chrome, and Adobe Photoshop are application software.

column6:
Match the following: Computer Security Term
1. Virus,
2. Worm,
3. Trojan,
4. Firewall. Meaning i. Self-replicating program, ii. Program that hides in legitimate software, iii. Malicious program that spreads, iv. Security barrier between networks.

I. ISRO successfully conducted the first uncrewed flight test of the Gaganyaan mission (TV-D1) in October 2023; the crewed mission is targeted for late 2026.

column14: Statement I is CORRECT: ISRO successfully conducted the first uncrewed flight test of the Gaganyaan mission, designated TV-D1 (Test Vehicle-D1), on 21 October 2023 from Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota. The mission tested the Crew Escape System (CES) at Mach 1.2. The crewed Gaganyaan mission is targeted for late 2026, with additional uncrewed tests planned before the human flight. Statement II is CORRECT: XPoSat (X-ray Polarimetry Satellite), India's first dedicated polarimetry mission, was launched on 1 January 2024 aboard PSLV-C58. The primary mission duration was 5 years. By early 2026, the mission had completed its primary observation phase, having studied 56 bright X-ray sources including black holes, neutron stars, and active galactic nuclei. Statement III is INCORRECT: GSAT-7B, the Navy's dedicated military communication satellite, was indeed planned and approved, but its operationalisation timeline was projected for 2026-27, not confirmed as operational by mid-2026. The satellite is designed to provide secure communication links for the Indian Navy across the Indian Ocean Region. As of mid-2026, it was still in the development/testing phase. This tests the critical ability to distinguish between confirmed milestones and projected timelines.

The formal induction of Kazakhstan and Malaysia as partner countries occurred in 2024-25. Statement II is CORRECT: The India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC) was announced at the G20 Summit in New Delhi (September 2023). By early 2026, pilot shipments via the UAE-Saudi Arabia-Israel route had commenced, testing the multimodal connectivity framework combining maritime and rail links. This represents a strategic economic initiative countering China's Belt and Road Initiative. Statement III is INCORRECT: There was no Nuclear Security Summit scheduled for Seoul in 2026. The Nuclear Security Summits were held irregularly — the last one was in Washington D.C. in 2016. The summits focus on securing nuclear materials and preventing nuclear terrorism. No new summit was announced for 2026. This tests awareness of ongoing vs. completed international processes.
