Which of the following pairs regarding major flagship schemes and their recent restructuring (2024-26) is/are correctly matched?
I. PM-KISAN — Annual instalment increased from ₹6,000 to ₹8,000 per farmer from FY 2025-26 onwards.
II. Ayushman Bharat — Expanded to cover all senior citizens above 70 years irrespective of income, with a dedicated ₹5 lakh cover.
III. PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana — Target revised to 3 crore rooftop solar installations by 2027 with enhanced central subsidy.
IV. National Digital Health Mission (ABHA) — Integrated with the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission for universal health records.

Choose the correct option:
column14: Pair I is INCORRECT: The PM-KISAN (Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi) scheme continues to provide Rs. 6,000 per year (in three instalments of Rs. 2,000 each) to eligible farmer families. There has been NO increase to Rs. 8,000 announced as of Budget 2025-26. The 20th instalment was released on 2 August 2025, and the 21st on 19 November 2025. The total amount transferred under the scheme crossed Rs. 3.69 lakh crore by late 2025. Pair II is CORRECT: Ayushman Bharat was expanded in Budget 2025-26 to cover all senior citizens above 70 years irrespective of income, with a dedicated Rs. 5 lakh cover per family per year. This was a major expansion of the world's largest government-funded health insurance scheme, adding approximately 4.5 crore senior citizen beneficiaries. Pair III is CORRECT: The PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana target was revised to 3 crore rooftop solar installations by 2027 (from the earlier 1 crore target), with enhanced central subsidy. The scheme provides free electricity up to 300 units per month to households and has seen significant uptake since its launch in February 2024. Pair IV is CORRECT: The National Digital Health Mission (NDHM), which issues Ayushman Bharat Health Accounts (ABHA IDs), was integrated with the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission for creating universal electronic health records (EHR). By 2025-26, over 70 crore ABHA IDs had been generated, enabling interoperability of health records across healthcare providers.

column6:
Which of the following statements regarding infrastructure, manufacturing, and employment schemes (2025-26) is/are correct?
I. The PM Mitra Mega Textile Parks scheme achieved full operationalisation of all 7 approved parks by March 2026, with two parks in Tamil Nadu and Gujarat commencing production.
II. Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme 2.0 was approved for sectors including leather, bicycle, and toys with an outlay of ₹22,000 crore.
III. The Employment Linked Incentive (ELI) Scheme introduced in Budget 2024-25 provided direct benefit transfers to first-time employees in the organised sector, with Phase II expanding coverage to EPFO-registered establishments with 10+ employees.

Choose the correct option:
column14: Statement I is INCORRECT: The PM Mitra Mega Textile Parks scheme, approved in 2021 with 7 parks, had NOT achieved full operationalisation by March 2026. While some parks made progress (Tamil Nadu and Gujarat parks were in advanced stages of development), full operationalisation with all parks commencing production was a longer-term target. The scheme faced implementation delays due to land acquisition and infrastructure challenges. This tests awareness of implementation lag versus announced targets. Statement II is CORRECT: PLI Scheme 2.0 was approved for additional sectors including leather, bicycle, and toys with an outlay of Rs. 22,000 crore in 2025-26. This expanded the PLI coverage to 14 sectors, aiming to boost domestic manufacturing and reduce import dependence in labour-intensive sectors. Statement III is CORRECT: The Employment Linked Incentive (ELI) Scheme was introduced in Budget 2024-25 to provide direct benefit transfers to first-time employees in the organised sector. Phase II expanded coverage to EPFO-registered establishments with 10+ employees (down from 20+ in Phase I), broadening the scheme's reach to smaller enterprises and increasing employment generation.

column6:
Consider the following pairs regarding financial sector developments and digital economy initiatives (2025-26):
I. UPI 2.0 enhancements — Introduction of "UPI Vouchers" for specific merchant categories and "UPI Credit Line" through pre-sanctioned bank credit.
II. Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) — India signed bilateral DPI agreements with 15 countries for exporting the India Stack (Aadhaar, UPI, DigiLocker).
III. RBI's Central Bank Digital Currency (e₹) — The retail e-rupee pilot crossed 10 million users with interoperability between banks achieved by Q1 2026.

Which of the above pairs are correctly matched?
column14: Pair I - UPI 2.0 (CORRECT): The NPCI introduced UPI Vouchers (pre-paid, pre-defined purpose vouchers for specific merchant categories like food, fuel, and travel) and UPI Credit Line (allowing users to access pre-sanctioned bank credit through UPI without a physical card). These enhancements were rolled out in 2024-25, significantly expanding UPI's utility beyond basic peer-to-peer transfers. Pair II - DPI (CORRECT): India signed bilateral Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) agreements with multiple countries for exporting the India Stack (Aadhaar, UPI, DigiLocker, Co-WIN). By 2025-26, India had DPI agreements with approximately 15 countries including Armenia, Sierra Leone, Togo, and others, positioning India as a global leader in digital public infrastructure. Pair III - e-Rupee (CORRECT): The RBI's retail Central Bank Digital Currency (e-rupee) pilot, launched in December 2022, crossed 10 million users by early 2026. Interoperability between participating banks was achieved by Q1 2026, allowing seamless e-rupee transactions across different bank wallets. The pilot covered both person-to-person (P2P) and person-to-merchant (P2M) transactions.

column6:
Consider the following statements regarding India's semiconductor and chip manufacturing ecosystem (2025-26):
I. The India Semiconductor Mission approved Micron Technology's assembly, test, and packaging facility in Gujarat, with commercial production commencing in early 2026.
II. Tata Electronics partnered with Taiwan's Powerchip Semiconductor Manufacturing Corporation (PSMC) to establish India's first indigenous fab in Dholera, Gujarat.
III. The Design Linked Incentive (DLI) Scheme was expanded in 2025 to cover 30 domestic semiconductor design companies, up from the initial
20.

Which of the above statements are correct?
column14: Statement I is CORRECT: The India Semiconductor Mission (ISM) approved Micron Technology's assembly, test, and packaging (ATMP) facility in Gujarat with an investment of $2.75 billion (approximately Rs. 22,500 crore). Commercial production commenced in early 2026, marking a significant milestone in India's semiconductor ecosystem development. The facility focuses on DRAM and NAND memory products. Statement II is CORRECT: Tata Electronics partnered with Taiwan's Powerchip Semiconductor Manufacturing Corporation (PSMC) to establish India's first indigenous semiconductor fabrication plant (fab) in Dholera, Gujarat. The fab targets 28nm technology nodes initially, with plans to scale down to more advanced nodes. This $11 billion project is India's most significant step toward semiconductor self-sufficiency. Statement III is INCORRECT: The Design Linked Incentive (DLI) Scheme was launched with an initial target of supporting 20 domestic semiconductor design companies. While expansion was discussed, there was no official announcement of expansion to 30 companies by mid-2026. The original target of 20 companies remained the official figure. This tests the ability to distinguish between speculated expansions and confirmed policy targets.

column6:
Which of the following pairs regarding 6G, satellite communication, and next-generation networks (2025-26) is/are correctly matched?
I. Bharat 6G Alliance — Launched the first set of 6G testbed specifications in partnership with IITs and IISc, targeting commercial rollout by 2030.
II. JioSpaceFiber — Received GMPCS (Global Mobile Personal Communication by Satellite) licence from DoT for satellite-based broadband services.
III. Starlink India — Began commercial operations in mid-2025 after receiving security clearance and establishing local data storage nodes. IV. 5G TSDSI standard — India's indigenous 5G standard was adopted by the ITU as a supplementary international standard for IoT applications.

Choose the correct option:
column14: Pair I - Bharat 6G Alliance (CORRECT): The Bharat 6G Alliance, launched in 2023, released its first set of 6G testbed specifications in partnership with IITs (IIT Madras, IIT Delhi, IIT Bombay) and IISc Bangalore. The alliance targets commercial rollout by 2030, with India aiming to contribute to global 6G standards and secure intellectual property rights in next-generation communications. Pair II - JioSpaceFiber (CORRECT): Reliance Jio's JioSpaceFiber received the GMPCS (Global Mobile Personal Communication by Satellite) licence from the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) for providing satellite-based broadband services. This enables Jio to offer high-speed internet in remote and rural areas via satellite connectivity, complementing its terrestrial 5G network. Pair III - Starlink India (CORRECT): Starlink India (SpaceX's satellite internet service) began commercial operations in mid-2025 after receiving security clearance from the Indian government and establishing local data storage nodes in India to comply with data localization requirements. The service offers low-latency broadband via a constellation of Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites. Pair IV - 5G TSDSI standard (INCORRECT): India's indigenous 5G standard developed by TSDSI (Telecommunications Standards Development Society, India) was proposed to the ITU for adoption as a supplementary international standard for IoT applications, but it had NOT been formally adopted by the ITU as of mid-2026. The proposal was still under review and discussion at international standards bodies. This tests awareness of ongoing processes versus completed milestones.

column6:
Consider the following statements about artificial intelligence, quantum computing, and emerging technologies in India (2025-26):
I. The IndiaAI Mission approved the procurement of 10,000 GPUs under the public-private partnership model to build indigenous AI compute capacity.
II. PARAM Siddhi-AI, India's first AI supercomputer, was ranked among the top 100 global supercomputers in the June 2025 TOP500 list.
III. The National Quantum Mission established the first Quantum Computing Applications Lab in partnership with AWS at IISc Bangalore.

Which of the above statements are correct?
column14: Statement I is CORRECT: The IndiaAI Mission approved the procurement of 10,000 GPUs under a public-private partnership model to build indigenous AI compute capacity. The mission, approved by the Union Cabinet in March 2024 with an outlay of Rs. 10,371.92 crore, aims to develop sovereign AI infrastructure, support startups, and promote ethical AI development in India. Statement II is CORRECT: PARAM Siddhi-AI, India's first AI supercomputer developed by C-DAC, was ranked among the top 100 global supercomputers in the June 2025 TOP500 list. It achieved a performance of 5.3 petaflops (Rmax) and is used for AI/ML research, drug discovery, climate modeling, and other compute-intensive applications. Statement III is INCORRECT: The Quantum Computing Applications Lab in partnership with AWS (Amazon Web Services) was established at IIT Bombay, NOT IISc Bangalore. This is a classic location trap frequently used in competitive exams. The lab provides researchers access to quantum computing hardware and simulators for developing quantum algorithms and applications.

column6:
Which of the following statements regarding defence technology, space applications, and dual-use technologies (2025-26) is/are correct?
I. ISRO's SSLV (Small Satellite Launch Vehicle) achieved operational status with three consecutive successful launches, including the dedicated military satellite TSAT-1A for Tata Advanced Systems.
II. The Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) successfully tested the Indigenous Technology Cruise Missile (ITCM) with an indigenous Manik turbofan engine. III. iDEX (Innovations for Defence Excellence) crossed the milestone of 400 contracts signed with startups and MSMEs for defence innovation.

Choose the correct option:
column14: Statement I is CORRECT: ISRO's SSLV (Small Satellite Launch Vehicle) achieved operational status with three consecutive successful launches. The TSAT-1A (Tata Satellite-1A), a dedicated military satellite for Tata Advanced Systems Limited (TASL), was successfully launched aboard SSLV-D3 in 2025. SSLV is designed for launching small satellites (up to 500kg to Low Earth Orbit) with minimal launch infrastructure and reduced turnaround time. Statement II is CORRECT: DRDO successfully tested the Indigenous Technology Cruise Missile (ITCM) powered by the indigenous Manik turbofan engine. The ITCM is a subsonic cruise missile with a range of approximately 1,000 km, designed for precision strikes against land targets. The Manik engine represents a significant achievement in indigenous propulsion systems for cruise missiles. Statement III is CORRECT: iDEX (Innovations for Defence Excellence), launched in 2018 under the Defence Innovation Organisation, crossed the milestone of 400 contracts signed with startups and MSMEs for defence innovation by 2025-26. iDEX provides funding, mentorship, and market access to startups developing defence technologies, fostering indigenisation and self-reliance in defence.

column6:
Consider the following pairs regarding health technology, biotechnology, and clean energy (2025-26):
I. CAR-T cell therapy — India's first indigenous CAR-T therapy "NexCAR19" (developed by IIT Bombay and Tata Memorial Hospital) received DCGI approval for commercial use in 2025.
II. Green Hydrogen Mission — India achieved the milestone of 1 million tonnes per annum green hydrogen production capacity by March 2026, ahead of the 2030 target.
III. PM-eBus Sewa Scheme — Deployed over 10,000 electric buses across 100 cities with indigenous battery technology from Olectra and JBM Auto.

Which of the above pairs are correctly matched?
column14: Pair I - CAR-T Therapy (CORRECT): India's first indigenous CAR-T cell therapy "NexCAR19", developed collaboratively by IIT Bombay and Tata Memorial Hospital, received DCGI (Drugs Controller General of India) approval for commercial use in 2025. NexCAR19 treats B-cell lymphomas and leukaemias at a fraction of the cost of imported CAR-T therapies (approximately Rs. 30-40 lakh vs. Rs. 3-4 crore for foreign therapies), making advanced cancer treatment accessible in India. Pair II - Green Hydrogen Mission (INCORRECT): India DID NOT achieve the milestone of 1 million tonnes per annum (MTPA) green hydrogen production capacity by March 2026. The actual installed capacity was significantly lower (approximately 0.5 MTPA by early 2026). The 1 MTPA target is projected for 2026-27 or 2027-28. The National Hydrogen Mission, launched in January 2023, aims for 5 MTPA by 2030. This tests the ability to distinguish between achieved and projected milestones. Pair III - PM-eBus Sewa (CORRECT): The PM-eBus Sewa Scheme deployed over 10,000 electric buses across 100 cities by 2025-26, with indigenous battery technology from manufacturers like Olectra GreenTech (a subsidiary of MEIL) and JBM Auto. The scheme promotes clean urban mobility and reduces carbon emissions from public transport.

column6:
Consider the following statements regarding India's manned space programme and Gaganyaan mission (2025-26):
I. The Gaganyaan-1 uncrewed mission, carrying the Vyommitra humanoid robot, was successfully launched aboard the LVM3-M3 vehicle in late 2025.
II. The Indian Air Force selected four astronaut candidates (Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla among them) for joint training with NASA under the Axiom Mission-4 for ISS exposure.
III. ISRO's TV-D2 in-flight abort test demonstrated the crew escape system at supersonic speeds, clearing the final hurdle before the crewed Gaganyaan flight.

Which of the above statements are correct?
column14: Statement I is INCORRECT: The Gaganyaan-1 uncrewed mission carrying Vyommitra was TV-D1, launched in October 2023, NOT late 2025. The 2025 uncrewed mission was a different configuration (likely TV-D2 or TV-D3) testing other systems. Vyommitra, the female humanoid robot, was part of the TV-D1 mission to test life support systems. This is a deliberate timeline trap mixing up different test vehicle missions. Statement II is CORRECT: The Indian Air Force selected four astronaut candidates for the Gaganyaan mission, including Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla. They underwent joint training with NASA under the Axiom Mission-4 for International Space Station (ISS) exposure. This Indo-US collaboration in human spaceflight represents a significant milestone in India's manned space programme. Statement III is CORRECT: ISRO's TV-D2 in-flight abort test successfully demonstrated the Crew Escape System (CES) at supersonic speeds, clearing a critical hurdle before the crewed Gaganyaan flight. The test validated the abort system's performance under maximum dynamic pressure (Max-Q) conditions, ensuring crew safety during launch emergencies.

column6:
Which of the following pairs regarding ISRO's satellite programmes and launch vehicles (2025-26) is/are correctly matched?
I. EOS-08 (Earth Observation Satellite) — Launched on SSLV-D4, carrying advanced thermal imaging payloads for agricultural and disaster monitoring.
II. GSAT-20 (GSAT-N2) — India's heaviest communication satellite (4,700 kg) launched aboard Falcon-9 under a commercial agreement with SpaceX.
III. NVS-02 (Navigation with Indian Constellation) — Second-generation NavIC satellite with L1 band signals for civilian smartphone compatibility.
IV. RISAT-1A (Radar Imaging Satellite) — All-weather surveillance satellite with 1-metre resolution, operated jointly by ISRO and the National Technical Research Organisation.

Choose the correct option:
column14: Pair I - EOS-08 (CORRECT): EOS-08 (Earth Observation Satellite-08) was launched aboard SSLV-D4, carrying advanced thermal imaging payloads for agricultural monitoring, disaster management, and land use mapping. EOS-08 is part of ISRO's Earth Observation Satellite series, providing high-resolution optical and thermal data for various civilian applications. Pair II - GSAT-20 (CORRECT): GSAT-20 (also designated GSAT-N2), India's heaviest communication satellite at approximately 4,700 kg, was launched aboard a SpaceX Falcon-9 rocket under a commercial launch agreement. Due to its weight exceeding GSLV Mk III's capacity for the required orbit, ISRO opted for the commercial Falcon-9 launch, marking a pragmatic approach to satellite deployment. Pair III - NVS-02 (CORRECT): NVS-02 (Navigation with Indian Constellation-02) is a second-generation NavIC (Navigation Indian Constellation) satellite featuring L1 band signals for civilian smartphone compatibility. The L1 band (1575.42 MHz) is the standard frequency used by GPS and other global navigation systems, enabling NavIC reception on commercial smartphones without specialized hardware. Pair IV - RISAT-1A (INCORRECT): RISAT-1A (Radar Imaging Satellite-1A) is indeed an all-weather surveillance satellite with 1-metre resolution, but it is NOT operated jointly by ISRO and NTRO. RISAT-1A is operated primarily by ISRO for defence and civilian applications, with data shared with defence agencies. The NTRO (National Technical Research Organisation) is a technical intelligence agency, not a satellite operator. This is a subtle institutional trap testing knowledge of organisational roles.

column6:
Consider the following statements about India's missile systems, strategic forces, and defence indigenisation (2025-26):
I. The Agni-V intercontinental ballistic missile was successfully test-fired with Multiple Independently Targetable Reentry Vehicle (MIRV) technology under the name "Agni-P Prime."
II. The Project 75I (P75I) conventional submarine programme saw the keel-laying of the first Scorpène-class submarine enhanced with Air-Independent Propulsion at Mazagon Dock.
III. The LCA Tejas Mk-2 programme received Initial Operational Clearance (IOC) in early 2026, with the first squadron planned for Sulur Air Force Station.

Which of the above statements are correct?
column14: Statement I is INCORRECT: The Agni-V intercontinental ballistic missile (ICBM) with a range of approximately 5,500 km was indeed successfully test-fired with MIRV (Multiple Independently Targetable Reentry Vehicle) technology. However, it was NOT renamed "Agni-P Prime." Agni-P is a separate, distinct medium-range ballistic missile (range ~1,000-2,000 km) developed for the Indian Navy and strategic forces. The MIRV-capable Agni-V retains its original designation. This is a deliberate nomenclature trap. Statement II is CORRECT: Project 75I (P75I), the conventional submarine programme, saw the keel-laying of the first Scorpène-class submarine enhanced with Air-Independent Propulsion (AIP) at Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Limited (MDL), Mumbai. The AIP system allows submarines to remain submerged for extended periods without surfacing for air, significantly enhancing stealth and operational endurance. Statement III is CORRECT: The LCA Tejas Mk-2 programme received Initial Operational Clearance (IOC) in early 2026, with the first squadron planned for Sulur Air Force Station in Tamil Nadu. The Tejas Mk-2 is an advanced variant of the indigenous Light Combat Aircraft, featuring enhanced avionics, radar, and weapons capability compared to the Mk-1 variant.

column6:
Which of the following statements regarding India's nuclear programme, strategic partnerships, and export control frameworks (2025-26) is/are correct?
I. The Kakrapar Atomic Power Station Unit 4 (700 MW PHWR) achieved criticality in 2025, making Gujarat the state with the highest installed nuclear capacity in India.
II. India formally joined the Wassenaar Arrangement on Export Controls for Conventional Arms and Dual-Use Goods and Technologies as its 43rd participating state.
III. The India-US civil nuclear deal saw the first shipment of US-origin uranium fuel arrive for the Tarapur Atomic Power Station under the renewed 123 Agreement protocols.

Choose the correct option:
column14: Statement I is CORRECT: Kakrapar Atomic Power Station Unit 4 (700 MW Pressurized Heavy Water Reactor - PHWR) achieved criticality in 2025. With this, Gujarat became the state with the highest installed nuclear capacity in India (Kakrapar Units 1-4 totaling 2,800 MW, plus other plants). Kakrapar-4 is part of India's indigenous PHWR programme and represents a significant step in expanding nuclear power generation. Statement II is INCORRECT: India joined the Wassenaar Arrangement in December 2017, NOT 2025. The Wassenaar Arrangement on Export Controls for Conventional Arms and Dual-Use Goods and Technologies is a multilateral export control regime. India became its 42nd participating state (not 43rd). This tests whether candidates confuse recent developments with historical facts. India's entry was a major diplomatic achievement during its NSG membership campaign. Statement III is CORRECT: The India-US civil nuclear deal saw the first shipment of US-origin uranium fuel arrive for the Tarapur Atomic Power Station under the renewed 123 Agreement protocols. This marked the operationalization of the landmark 2008 Indo-US nuclear deal, ending India's nuclear isolation and enabling fuel imports for safeguarded reactors.

column6:
Consider the following pairs regarding defence technology missions, cyber and space domains, and emerging strategic capabilities (2025-26):
I. Defence Space Agency (DSA) — Operationalised the Space Situational Awareness (SSA) control centre at Bengaluru for tracking debris and hostile satellites.
II. Indian Navy's 'Swavlamban' initiative — Inducted the first indigenous heavy-duty underwater drone (Autonomous Underwater Vehicle) "Neerakshi" for mine countermeasures.
III. Bharat Shakti — The tri-service exercise held in Pokhran in 2025 integrated space-based assets, drone swarms, and cyber warfare elements for the first time.

Which of the above pairs are correctly matched?
column14: Pair I - DSA SSA Centre (CORRECT): The Defence Space Agency (DSA) operationalised the Space Situational Awareness (SSA) control centre at Bengaluru for tracking space debris, monitoring hostile satellites, and protecting Indian space assets. The SSA centre provides real-time tracking of objects in Earth's orbit, collision avoidance warnings, and intelligence on adversarial space activities. Pair II - Swavlamban & Neerakshi (CORRECT): The Indian Navy's 'Swavlamban' initiative (self-reliance in naval technology) inducted the first indigenous heavy-duty Autonomous Underwater Vehicle (AUV) "Neerakshi" for mine countermeasures. Developed by the Naval Science and Technological Laboratory (NSTL), Neerakshi can detect and neutralize underwater mines, enhancing the Navy's littoral warfare capabilities without risking human divers. Pair III - Bharat Shakti (CORRECT): Bharat Shakti, the tri-service exercise held in Pokhran, Rajasthan in 2025, integrated space-based assets, drone swarms, and cyber warfare elements for the first time in a major Indian military exercise. The exercise demonstrated joint operations capabilities across the Army, Navy, and Air Force, with emphasis on multi-domain warfare including space, cyber, and electronic warfare domains.

column6:
Consider the following statements regarding the Preamble of the Indian Constitution and its judicial interpretation:
I. The Supreme Court in the Berubari Union Case (1960) held that the Preamble is not a part of the Constitution and cannot be a source of substantive power.
II. The Supreme Court in Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973) overruled the Berubari view and held that the Preamble is an integral part of the Constitution, subject to amendment under Article 368.
III. The Supreme Court in Dr. Balram Singh v. Union of India (2024) dismissed petitions challenging the inclusion of "Socialist" and "Secular" in the Preamble, holding that these values were inherent in the Constitution's ethos from the beginning.

Which of the above statements are correct?
column14: Statement I is CORRECT: In the Berubari Union Case (1960), the Supreme Court held that the Preamble is NOT a part of the Constitution and cannot be a source of substantive power. The case arose from the Indo-Pakistan agreement on the Berubari Union territory exchange. The Court ruled that the Preamble is merely a key to open the mind of the makers of the Constitution but does not confer any legal rights or obligations. Statement II is CORRECT: In Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973), the 13-judge Constitution Bench overruled the Berubari view and held that the Preamble is an integral part of the Constitution. The Court ruled that the Preamble is subject to amendment under Article 368, but the basic structure of the Constitution (including the Preamble's core values) cannot be destroyed. This landmark judgment established the "Basic Structure Doctrine." Statement III is CORRECT: In Dr. Balram Singh v. Union of India (2024), the Supreme Court dismissed petitions challenging the inclusion of "Socialist" and "Secular" in the Preamble (added by the 42nd Amendment, 1976). The Court held that these values were inherent in the Constitution's ethos from the beginning, even before their explicit textual inclusion. The 42nd Amendment merely made explicit what was already implicit in the Constitution's framework.

column6:
Consider the following statements regarding Fundamental Rights under Part III of the Indian Constitution:
I. Article 19 guarantees six freedoms to all persons, including both citizens and non-citizens, but these freedoms are subject to reasonable restrictions under clauses (2) to (6).
II. Article 19(1)(a) guarantees freedom of speech and expression, which can be reasonably restricted under Article 19(2) on grounds including public order, decency, morality, and sovereignty and integrity of India.
III. The right to property was removed from the list of Fundamental Rights by the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978, and was made a constitutional right under Article 300A.

Which of the above statements are correct?
column14:
Statement I is INCORRECT: Article 19 guarantees six freedoms (originally seven, before the 44th Amendment removed the right to property) to CITIZENS ONLY, NOT to "all persons" including non-citizens. The freedoms under Article 19(1) are:
(a) freedom of speech and expression,
(b) assembly,
(c) association,
(d) movement, (e) residence, and (g) profession/occupation. Aliens/foreigners cannot claim these rights. Non-citizens are protected under Article 14 (Equality before law) and Article 21 (Right to life and personal liberty), but NOT under Article
19. Statement II is CORRECT: Article 19(1)(a) guarantees freedom of speech and expression. This can be reasonably restricted under Article 19(2) on grounds including: sovereignty and integrity of India, security of the State, friendly relations with foreign States, public order, decency, morality, contempt of court, defamation, and incitement to an offence. The restrictions must be "reasonable" and fall within the specified grounds. Statement III is CORRECT: The right to property was removed from the list of Fundamental Rights by the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978. It was made a constitutional right under Article 300A, which states that "No person shall be deprived of his property save by authority of law." Unlike Fundamental Rights, Article 300A is not enforceable against private individuals and does not require compensation for acquisition.

column6:
Consider the following statements regarding Fundamental Duties under Article 51A:
I. The Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.
II. Article 51A(k) mandates every parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to his child or ward between the age of 6 and 14 years, which was added by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002.
III. The Fundamental Duties are enforceable by courts through writs under Article 32 and Article 226, similar to Fundamental Rights.

Which of the above statements are correct?
column14: Statement I is CORRECT: The Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee (1976). Originally 10 duties were added via Article 51A. The Swaran Singh Committee recommended incorporating duties to balance the emphasis on rights with corresponding responsibilities of citizens. Statement II is CORRECT: Article 51A(k) mandates every parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to his child or ward between the age of 6 and 14 years. This was added by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002, which also inserted Article 21A (Right to Education as a Fundamental Right). The 86th Amendment made education a concurrent responsibility of the State and parents. Statement III is INCORRECT: Fundamental Duties are NON-JUSTICIABLE in nature. They CANNOT be enforced through writs under Article 32 or Article 226, unlike Fundamental Rights. However, Parliament may enforce them through suitable legislation. For example, the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971 enforces the duty to respect the National Flag and National Anthem. Courts may also consider Fundamental Duties while interpreting laws (as held in various judgments).

column6:
Consider the following statements regarding the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) under Part IV of the Indian Constitution:
I. The DPSPs are borrowed from the Constitution of Ireland and are non-justiciable in nature, meaning they cannot be enforced by any court.
II. Article 44 (Uniform Civil Code) and Article 48 (Organisation of Agriculture and Animal Husbandry) are classified as Liberal-Intellectual Principles among the DPSPs.
III. The Supreme Court in Minerva Mills v. Union of India (1980) held that there is no conflict between Fundamental Rights and DPSPs; they are complementary to each other and together constitute the core of the Constitution.

Which of the above statements are correct?
column14:
Statement I is CORRECT: The DPSPs are borrowed from the Constitution of Ireland (Article 45 of the Irish Constitution). They are non-justiciable in nature, meaning they cannot be enforced by any court (Article 37). DPSPs are directives to the State for governance and policy-making, guiding the legislature and executive in enacting laws and formulating policies. Statement II is INCORRECT: While Article 44 (Uniform Civil Code) is indeed classified as a Liberal-Intellectual Principle, Article 48 (Organisation of Agriculture and Animal Husbandry) is a Gandhian Principle, NOT a Liberal-Intellectual Principle. The classification is: Gandhian Principles: Articles 40 (Village Panchayats), 43 (Living wage), 43B (Worker participation), 46 (Scheduled Castes/Tribes), 47 (Nutrition/health), 48 (Agriculture/animal husbandry). Liberal-Intellectual Principles: Articles 44 (UCC), 45 (Early childhood care), 50 (Separation of judiciary), 51 (International peace). Socialist Principles: Articles 38, 39, 39A, 41, 42,
43. Statement III is CORRECT: In Minerva Mills v. Union of India (1980), the Supreme Court held that there is no conflict between Fundamental Rights and DPSPs; they are complementary to each other and together constitute the core of the Constitution. The Court ruled that the harmony and balance between FRs and DPSPs is part of the Constitution's basic structure, which cannot be destroyed.

column6:
Consider the following statements regarding the relationship between Fundamental Rights, Fundamental Duties, and Directive Principles of State Policy:
I. The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 added four new DPSPs — Article 39 (opportunities for healthy development of children), Article 39A (equal justice and free legal aid), Article 43A (participation of workers in management), and Article 48A (protection of environment and wildlife).
II. Article 31C, as originally inserted by the 25th Amendment Act, 1971, gave primacy to DPSPs in Articles 39(b) and 39(c) over Fundamental Rights under Articles 14, 19, and
31.
III. The Supreme Court in Golak Nath v. State of Punjab (1967) held that Fundamental Rights are transcendental and cannot be amended by Parliament under Article 368.

Which of the above statements are correct?
column14:
Statement I is CORRECT: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 added four new DPSPs: Article 39 — Equal pay for equal work for men and women; protection of children against exploitation. Article 39A — Equal justice and free legal aid. Article 43A — Participation of workers in management of industries. Article 48A — Protection and improvement of environment and safeguarding of forests and wildlife. Statement II is CORRECT: Article 31C, as originally inserted by the 25th Amendment Act, 1971, gave primacy to DPSPs in Articles 39(b) and 39(c) (equal distribution of material resources and prevention of concentration of wealth) over Fundamental Rights under Articles 14, 19, and
31. However, in Kesavananda Bharati (1973), the Supreme Court ruled that while Parliament can amend the Constitution, it cannot destroy the "basic structure," and the judiciary retains the power of judicial review. Statement III is CORRECT: In Golak Nath v. State of Punjab (1967), the Supreme Court (11-judge bench) held that Fundamental Rights are transcendental and cannot be amended by Parliament under Article 368. This was a landmark judgment that was later partially overruled by Kesavananda Bharati (1973), which established that Fundamental Rights CAN be amended, but not in a way that destroys the Constitution's basic structure.

column6:
Consider the following statements regarding the Disaster Management Act, 2005 and institutional framework in India:
I. The Disaster Management Act, 2005 provides for the establishment of the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) under the Chairmanship of the Prime Minister of India, with a maximum of nine members including a Vice-Chairperson.
II. Under the Act, the State Disaster Management Authority (SDMA) is headed by the Chief Minister of the State, and the District Disaster Management Authority (DDMA) is headed by the District Collector or Deputy Commissioner.
III. The Act defines "disaster" to mean a catastrophe, mishap, calamity or grave occurrence arising from natural or man-made causes, but excludes events caused by hostile acts of foreign countries or armed rebellion.

Which of the above statements are correct?
column14: Statement I is CORRECT: The Disaster Management Act, 2005 provides for the establishment of the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) under the Chairmanship of the Prime Minister of India, with a maximum of nine members including a Vice-Chairperson. The NDMA is the apex body for disaster management in India, responsible for laying down policies, plans, and guidelines for disaster management. Statement II is CORRECT: Under the Act, the State Disaster Management Authority (SDMA) is headed by the Chief Minister of the State, and the District Disaster Management Authority (DDMA) is headed by the District Collector or Deputy Commissioner, with the elected representative of the local authority as Co-Chairperson. This creates a three-tier institutional framework: national, state, and district levels. Statement III is INCORRECT: The Act's definition of "disaster" is BROAD and INCLUSIVE. It does NOT exclude events caused by hostile acts of foreign countries or armed rebellion. Section 2(d) defines disaster as "a catastrophe, mishap, calamity or grave occurrence in any area, arising from natural or man-made causes..." The definition covers ALL events causing substantial loss of life or destruction of property, including those caused by hostile acts or armed rebellion. The COVID-19 pandemic was also notified as a disaster under this Act.

column6:
Consider the following statements regarding disaster classification and the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction (2015-2030):
I. The Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015-2030 is the successor to the Hyogo Framework for Action (HFA) 2005-2015, and was adopted at the Third UN World Conference on Disaster Risk Reduction held in Sendai, Japan.
II. The Sendai Framework identifies four priorities for action:
(i) Understanding disaster risk,
(ii) Strengthening disaster risk governance,
(iii) Investing in disaster risk reduction for resilience, and
(iv) Enhancing disaster preparedness for effective response and to "Build Back Better" in recovery, rehabilitation and reconstruction.
III. Under India's classification, disasters are categorized into natural disasters (earthquakes, floods, cyclones, landslides, droughts) and man-made disasters (chemical/industrial, nuclear, biological, mine disasters, and oil spills), with COVID-19 pandemic being notified as a "disaster" under the DM Act, 2005.

Which of the above statements are correct?
column14: Statement I is CORRECT: The Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015-2030 is indeed the successor to the Hyogo Framework for Action (HFA) 2005-2015. It was adopted at the Third UN World Conference on Disaster Risk Reduction held in Sendai, Japan in March 2015. The Sendai Framework is a 15-year, voluntary, non-binding agreement that recognizes that the State has the primary role in reducing disaster risk, but that responsibility should be shared with other stakeholders including local government, the private sector, and other institutions. Statement II is CORRECT: The Sendai Framework identifies four priorities for action: (1) Understanding disaster risk — comprehensive risk assessment and data; (2) Strengthening disaster risk governance — institutional frameworks and coordination; (3) Investing in disaster risk reduction for resilience — public and private investment; (4) Enhancing disaster preparedness for effective response and to "Build Back Better" — recovery, rehabilitation, and reconstruction. Statement III is CORRECT: Under India's classification, disasters are categorized into Natural disasters (earthquakes, floods, cyclones, landslides, droughts, tsunamis) and Man-made disasters (chemical/industrial, nuclear, biological, mine disasters, oil spills, building collapse). The COVID-19 pandemic was indeed notified as a "disaster" under the DM Act, 2005 by the Ministry of Home Affairs, enabling the invocation of disaster management protocols for pandemic response.

Consider the following statements regarding India's climate change mitigation and adaptation efforts:
I. The National Adaptation Fund for Climate Change (NAFCC) was established in 2015 to support adaptation activities in the States and Union Territories that are particularly vulnerable to the adverse effects of climate change.
II. The Green Climate Fund (GCF) is an operating entity of the financial mechanism of the UNFCCC and the Paris Agreement, and India has accessed GCF funding for projects related to coastal resilience and renewable energy.
III. The National Mission for a Green India (GIM), one of the eight missions under NAPCC, aims to increase forest/tree cover on 5 million hectares of forest/non-forest lands and improve quality of forest cover on another 5 million hectares.

Which of the above statements are correct?
column14: Statement I is CORRECT: The National Adaptation Fund for Climate Change (NAFCC) was established in 2015 under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC). It supports adaptation activities in States and UTs particularly vulnerable to climate change effects. The fund finances state-level adaptation projects in areas like agriculture, water resources, forestry, and coastal management. It is primarily funded through a levy on coal (National Clean Energy Fund contributions). Statement II is CORRECT: The Green Climate Fund (GCF) is an operating entity of the financial mechanism of both the UNFCCC and the Paris Agreement. India has accessed GCF funding for projects related to coastal resilience (e.g., enhancing climate resilience of India's coastal communities) and renewable energy (e.g., solar power projects). The GCF was established in 2010 to assist developing countries in adaptation and mitigation practices to counter climate change. Statement III is CORRECT: The National Mission for a Green India (GIM), one of the eight missions under NAPCC, aims to increase forest/tree cover on 5 million hectares of forest/non-forest lands and improve quality of forest cover on another 5 million hectares. It also aims to enhance ecosystem services including carbon sequestration, biodiversity conservation, and hydrological services. The mission was approved in 2014 with a 10-year implementation period and is implemented by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.

Consider the following statements regarding disaster management in Jammu & Kashmir and recent developments:
I. The Jammu & Kashmir State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) was constituted under the Disaster Management Act, 2005, and is responsible for responding to disasters including earthquakes, floods, landslides, and snow avalanches which are common in the Himalayan region.
II. The Sendai Framework's seven global targets include substantial reduction of disaster mortality, substantial reduction of people affected, substantial reduction of direct disaster economic loss, and substantial reduction of disaster damage to critical infrastructure.
III. India's National Disaster Management Plan (NDMP), 2019 aligns with the Sendai Framework and covers all phases of disaster management — prevention, mitigation, preparedness, response, and recovery — with specific focus on climate change adaptation and disaster risk reduction.

Which of the above statements are correct?
column14: Statement I is CORRECT: The Jammu & Kashmir State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) was constituted under the Disaster Management Act, 2005. It is responsible for responding to disasters including earthquakes, floods, landslides, and snow avalanches — all common in the Himalayan region of J&K. The SDRF works under the State Disaster Management Authority and is equipped with specialized mountain rescue equipment, avalanche rescue gear, and high-altitude medical support. Statement II is CORRECT: The Sendai Framework's seven global targets (2015-2030) include: substantial reduction of global disaster mortality; substantial reduction of number of affected people globally; reduction of direct disaster economic loss in relation to global GDP; substantial reduction of disaster damage to critical infrastructure and disruption of basic services; substantial increase in number of countries with national and local disaster risk reduction strategies; substantial enhancement of international cooperation to developing countries; and substantial increase in availability of and access to multi-hazard early warning systems. Statement III is CORRECT: India's National Disaster Management Plan (NDMP), 2019 aligns with the Sendai Framework and covers all phases of disaster management: prevention, mitigation, preparedness, response, and recovery. It has specific focus on climate change adaptation and disaster risk reduction, integrating disaster management with sustainable development goals. The NDMP was revised in 2019 to incorporate lessons from the 2018 Kerala floods and other recent disasters.

column6: Consider the following statements about prehistoric Kashmir: S1: The Burzahom site reveals pit-dwelling structures. S2: Neolithic tools were found at Gufkral. S3: The name "Kashmir" derives from sage Kashyapa. Which are correct?
column14: All three statements are correct. Burzahom is known for pit-dwelling structures, Gufkral yielded Neolithic tools, and the name Kashmir is believed to derive from sage Kashyapa.

column6:

column7: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A
column8: Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
column9: A is true but R is false

4. Sangramaraja.

Select the correct code:
column14: Kanishka of the Kushana dynasty held the 4th Buddhist Council, Lalitaditya Muktapida was the greatest Karkota ruler, Avantivarman of the Utpala dynasty introduced land reforms, and Sangramaraja belonged to the Lohara dynasty.

column6: Which of the following is NOT correct regarding the Karkota Dynasty?
column8: Lalitaditya built the Martand Sun Temple
column9: It was overthrown by the Utpala Dynasty in 855 AD
column10: Jayapida was its most expansionist ruler
column14: Statements A, B, and C are historically true facts. Durlabhavardhana established the empire, Lalitaditya commissioned the Martand Sun Temple, and Avantivarman overthrew them in 855 AD. Statement D is false because Lalitaditya Muktapida, not Jayapida, was the most expansionist ruler of the Karkota dynasty, making D the correct choice.

column6: Consider the following statements about the Shah Mir Dynasty: S1: Shah Mir founded the Sultanate in 1339. S2: Sikandar Butshikan destroyed the Martand Temple. S3: Zain-ul-Abidin was called "Budshah" (Great King). Which are correct?
column14: All three statements are correct. Shah Mir founded the Sultanate in 1339, Sikandar Butshikan earned the title "Iconoclast" for destroying temples including Martand, and Zain-ul-Abidin was revered as Budshah for his tolerant policies.

column6: Which of the following is NOT a correct chronological order?
column7: Maurya to Kushana to Karkota to Utpala
column8: Lohara to Shah Mir to Chak to Mughal
column9: Utpala to Lohara to Shah Mir to Afghan
column10: Naga to Maurya to Karkota to Chak
column14: The correct sequence should include Kushana, Utpala, Lohara, and Shah Mir between the Karkota and Chak dynasties. The Naga dynasty preceded the Mauryas, but multiple dynasties are missing between Karkota and Chak.

column6:
Assertion (A): The Chak Dynasty was the last independent Kashmiri Muslim rule.
Reason (R): Yusuf Shah Chak was defeated by Akbar in 1586.

Select the correct code:
column7: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A
column8: Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
column9: A is true but R is false
column10: A is false but R is true
column14: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A. The Chak Dynasty was indeed the last independent Muslim rule, and its defeat by Akbar in 1586 marked the end of independent Kashmiri rule.

column6: Consider the following statements about Mughal Kashmir: S1: Akbar annexed Kashmir in 1586. S2: Jahangir built the Shalimar and Nishat gardens. S3: Aurangzeb imposed Jizya on Kashmiri Pandits. Which are correct?
column14: Akbar annexed Kashmir in 1586, Jahangir built the  Shalimar Bagh and not Nishat Bagh which was built by Asif Khan during the reign of Shah Jahan, and Aurangzeb imposed Jizya on Kashmiri Pandits during his reign.

column6:
Match the following: 
A. Afghan Rule - 1. Atta Mohammad Khan's tyranny, 
B. Sikh Period - 2. Governor Moti Ram's appointment, 
C. Ranjit Singh - 3. Treaty of Lahore (1846), 
D. Gulab Singh - 4. Treaty of Amritsar. 
Select the correct code:
column14: Atta Mohammad Khan was an Afghan tyrant, the Sikh period saw Moti Ram's appointment as governor, Ranjit Singh's death led to the Treaty of Lahore in 1846, and Gulab Singh became Maharaja through the Treaty of Amritsar.

column6: Which of the following is NOT correct regarding post-independence J&K?
column7: Sheikh Abdullah launched the Quit Kashmir movement in 1946
column8: The 1952 Delhi Agreement was between Nehru and Bakshi Ghulam Mohammad
column9: The 1975 Indira-Sheikh Accord restored Abdullah as Chief Minister
column14: The 1952 Delhi Agreement was signed between Jawaharlal Nehru and Sheikh Abdullah, not Bakshi Ghulam Mohammad. Bakshi succeeded Abdullah after his dismissal in 1953.

column6: Consider the following statements about J&K physiography: S1: The Trans-Himalayan zone includes Ladakh and Zanskar. S2: The Greater Himalayas contain the Nun-Kun peaks. S3: The Outer Himalayas include the Siwalik ranges in Jammu. Which are correct?
column14: All three statements are correct. The Trans-Himalayan zone comprises Ladakh and Zanskar, the Nun-Kun peaks are in the Greater Himalayas, and the Siwalik ranges form the Outer Himalayas in Jammu.

column6:
Assertion (A): The Jhelum River is called the "lifeline of Kashmir."
Reason (R): It is the only river that flows entirely within the Kashmir Valley.

Select the correct code:
column7: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A
column8: Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
column9: A is true but R is false
column10: A is false but R is true
column14: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A. The Jhelum is called the lifeline because it flows entirely within the Kashmir Valley, supporting agriculture, transport, and livelihoods.

column6: Which of the following is NOT correct regarding J&K lakes?
column7: Pangong Tso is an endorheic lake shared with China
column8: Tso Moriri is a Ramsar site at 4,522 metres
column9: Dal Lake is a tectonic lake formed by faulting
column10: Wular Lake is fed by the Jhelum River
column14: Dal Lake is a fluvial/oxbow lake formed by river meandering, not a tectonic lake formed by faulting. It was formed by the Jhelum's alluvial deposits.

column6:
Match

2. Largest high-altitude lake in India, C. Dal -
3. Floating gardens and houseboats, D. Mansar -
4. Freshwater, pilgrimage site.

Select the correct code:
column14: Pangong Tso is brackish and freezes in winter, Tso Moriri is the largest high-altitude lake in India, Dal is famous for floating gardens and houseboats, and Mansar is a freshwater pilgrimage site in Jammu.

column6: Consider the following statements about J&K climate: S1: Ladakh receives less than 10 cm annual rainfall. S2: Jammu has a subtropical climate with hot summers. S3: The Kashmir Valley has a temperate climate with four distinct seasons. Which are correct?
column14: All three statements are correct. Ladakh is a cold desert with negligible rainfall, Jammu has a subtropical climate, and the Kashmir Valley experiences a temperate climate with four distinct seasons.

column6: Which of the following is NOT correct regarding J&K soils?
column7: Karewas are loess deposits of Pleistocene age
column8: Glacial soils are found in the Zanskar range
column9: Red soils are predominant in the Jammu plains
column10: Alluvial soils cover the Kashmir Valley floor
column14: Jammu plains have predominantly alluvial and loamy soils, not red soils. Red soils are typical of tropical regions with high iron oxide content, not the Jammu plains.

column6:
Assertion (A): The Kashmir stag (Hangul) is critically endangered.
Reason (R): Its population has declined due to habitat fragmentation and poaching.

Select the correct code:
column7: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A
column8: Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
column9: A is true but R is false
column10: A is false but R is true
column14: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A. The Hangul is listed as critically endangered by the IUCN, primarily due to habitat fragmentation in Dachigam and persistent poaching.

column6:
Match the following: A. Chiru -
1. Ladakh, hunted for shahtoosh, B. Markhor -
2. Kishtwar National Park, C. Blue Sheep -
3. Hemis National Park, D. Snow Leopard -
4. Dachigam National Park.

Select the correct code:
column14: Chiru (Tibetan antelope) is found in Ladakh and hunted for shahtoosh wool, Markhor is found in Kishtwar, Blue Sheep (Bharal) is found in Hemis, and Snow Leopard is found across high-altitude regions including Dachigam.

column6: Consider the following statements about J&K biodiversity: S1: The Great Himalayan National Park is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. S2: Hemis National Park is the largest national park in India. S3: Dachigam was initially established to ensure clean water supply to Srinagar. Which are correct?
column14: All three statements are correct. GHNP is a UNESCO WHS, Hemis is the largest national park in India by area, and Dachigam was originally a protected area to preserve the watershed for Srinagar's water supply.

column6: Which of the following is NOT correct?
column7: The Chenab River is formed by the confluence of Chandra and Bhaga
column8: The Ravi River originates in the Kullu Hills of Himachal Pradesh
column9: The Indus River flows through the Ladakh region before entering Pakistan
column10: The Tawi River is a tributary of the Jhelum River
column14: The Tawi River is a tributary of the Chenab River, not the Jhelum. It flows through Jammu city and joins the Chenab near the Pakistan border.

column6: Consider the following statements about the Act's preamble: S1: It reorganises the state of Jammu & Kashmir. S2: It establishes two Union Territories. S3: It repeals the J&K Constitution of 1957. Which are correct?
column14: All three statements are correct. The Act reorganises the erstwhile state into two UTs, establishes the J&K UT and Ladakh UT, and effectively repeals the J&K Constitution of 1957.

column6:

column7: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A
column8: Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A

column14: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A. The special status was removed through the Presidential Order abrogating Article 370, which enabled the Reorganisation Act to be implemented.

column6: Which of the following is NOT correct regarding the Act's territorial provisions?
column9: Kargil and Leh are the districts of Ladakh UT
column10: The J&K UT has 107 seats in the Legislative Assembly
column14: The J&K UT has 114 seats in the Legislative Assembly, not 107. The 107 figure was the previous number before the Act increased it by 7 seats for displaced persons.

column6: Consider the following statements about the Act's administrative structure: S1: The Administrator of J&K UT is called Lieutenant Governor. S2: The LG of Ladakh acts independently of the J&K LG. S3: Both UTs have a common High Court at Srinagar. Which are correct?
column14: All three statements are correct. The J&K UT Administrator is designated as Lieutenant Governor, Ladakh has its own independent LG, and both UTs share the common High Court of J&K and Ladakh at Srinagar.

column6: Which of the following is NOT correct regarding the Act's legislative provisions?
column7: The J&K UT Assembly can make laws on State List subjects
column8: The Parliament has exclusive power on Union List subjects
column9: The Concurrent List applies to J&K UT as in other states
column10: The LG can promulgate ordinances when Assembly is not in session
column14: The Concurrent List applies to J&K UT as in other Union Territories, not as in states. The LG has special powers in J&K UT that differ from full state status.

column6:

Select the correct code:
column7: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A
column8: Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A

column10: A is false but R is true
column14: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A. The Act increased seats from 107 to 114, specifically creating 7 seats for displaced persons from Pakistan-occupied Kashmir.

Select the correct code:
column14: Schedule I defines the Seats in Rajya Sabha J&K UT territory, Schedule II lists Parliamentary Constituencies, Schedule III lists Assembly Constituencies, and Schedule IV contains oaths and affirmations.

column6: Consider the following statements about the Nilamata Purana: S1: It describes the sacred geography of Kashmir. S2: It mentions the six traditional seasons of Kashmir. S3: It prescribes the worship of Nagas as protectors of the valley. Which are correct?
column14: All three statements are correct. The Nilamata Purana is a 6th-7th century text that describes Kashmir's sacred geography, its six traditional seasons (Shad Ritu), and the worship of Nagas as divine protectors of the valley.

column6:
Assertion (A): The 4th Buddhist Council held under Kanishka was significant for Kashmir.
Reason (R): It resulted in the division of Buddhism into Hinayana and Mahayana sects.

Select the correct code:
column7: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A
column8: Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
column9: A is true but R is false
column10: A is false but R is true
column14: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A. The 4th Buddhist Council held in Kashmir under Kanishka was historically significant as it formally led to the schism between Hinayana and Mahayana Buddhism, establishing Kashmir as a major Buddhist center.

column6:
Match

List-I (Ruler) with

List-II (Contribution/Association): A. Lalitaditya Muktapida -
1. Rajatarangini's most celebrated hero, B. Avantivarman -
2. Suyya's drainage of Kashmir marshes, C. Jayapida -
3. Karkota dynasty's last great ruler, D. Durlabhaka -
4. Pratapaditya's dynasty restoration.

Select the correct code:
column14: The correct sequence is A-1, B-2, C-4, D-3, matching Option B. Lalitaditya Muktapida is the central epic hero of Kalhana's Rajatarangini (A-1). Avantivarman famously utilized his brilliant engineer Suyya to control devastating floods by draining the Valley's valley marshes (B-2). Durlabhaka was famously styled as Pratapaditya II (D-3). Jayapida Vinayaditya stands historically as the Karkota dynasty's last great imperial ruler who patronized scholars and attempted to recreate his grandfather's conquests (C-4).

column6: Which of the following is NOT correct regarding the Lohara Dynasty?
column7: It was founded by Sangramaraja after the Utpala collapse
column8: Harsha was its most intellectually inclined ruler
column9: It ended with the invasion of Zulchu in 1320
column10: It maintained the tradition of Rajatarangini chronicles
column14: Statements A, B, and D are historically accurate. The Lohara dynasty actually ended around 1171-1175 CE. The devastating invasion of Zulchu (Dulacha) occurred much later in 1320 CE, targeting the subsequent Dev dynasty of Kashmir, making statement C the incorrect fact.

column6:
Consider the following statements about Sikandar Butshikan: 
S1: He earned the epithet "Butshikan" for destroying Hindu temples. 
S2: He imposed Jizya on non-Muslims during his reign. 
S3: He completely banned the usage of Persian as the official court language Which are correct?
column14: Statements S1 and S2 are historically correct. Sikandar earned the title "Butshikan" (Iconoclast) for his mass destruction of temples and icons, and he famously introduced the Jizya tax on non-Muslims in Kashmir. Statement S3 is completely false because Sikandar actually promoted Persian and accelerated its adoption in the state administration, making Option A the correct choice.

column6: Which of the following is NOT a correct pairing?
column7: Zain-ul-Abidin - Tolerant policies and revival of Sanskrit
column8: Yusuf Shah Chak - Patron of Kashmiri poetry and music
column9: Habba Khatoon - Queen of Yusuf Shah Chak
column10: Akbar's annexation - End of the Chak dynasty in 1592
column14: Akbar annexed Kashmir in 1586, not 1592.

column6:
Assertion (A): The Afghan rule in Kashmir (1752-1819) is considered the darkest period.
Reason (R): The Afghans systematically destroyed Kashmir's shawl industry and imposed heavy taxation.

Select the correct code:
column7: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A
column8: Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
column9: A is true but R is false
column10: A is false but R is true
column14: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A. The Afghan period (1752-1819) under governors like Atta Mohammad Khan is considered the darkest due to systematic destruction of the shawl industry, extortionate taxation, and brutal oppression, which explains why it is termed the darkest period.

column6: Consider the following statements about the 1931 Kashmir Agitation: S1: It began with the trial of Abdul Qadeer Khan in Srinagar. S2: It led to the establishment of the Glancy Commission. S3: It forced Maharaja Hari Singh to introduce the Praja Sabha. Which are correct?
column14: All three statements are correct. The 1931 agitation began with Abdul Qadeer Khan's trial, led to the Glancy Commission (1932) to investigate grievances, and compelled Hari Singh to establish the Praja Sabha (1934) as a legislative body.

column6:
Match the following: A. Quit Kashmir Movement - 1. 1946, B. Instrument of Accession - 2. 26 October 1947, C. Delhi Agreement - 3. 1952, D. Sheikh Abdullah's dismissal - 4. 9 August 1953.

Select the correct code:
column14: The Quit Kashmir Movement was launched in 1946, the Instrument of Accession was signed on 26 October 1947, the Delhi Agreement was signed in 1952, and Sheikh Abdullah was dismissed on 9 August 1953.

column6: Which of the following is NOT correct regarding the 1975 Indira-Sheikh Accord?
column7: It restored Sheikh Abdullah as Chief Minister of J&K
column8: It retained the nomenclature of Prime Minister for J&K head
column9: It accepted the supremacy of the Indian Constitution in J&K
column10: It marked the end of the Plebiscite Front
column14: Statement B is historically incorrect, making it the correct selection. The nomenclature of Prime Minister had already been changed to Chief Minister via the 6th Amendment to the J&K Constitution in 1965. The 1975 Accord upheld this change rather than retaining the title of Prime Minister. The accord successfully restored Sheikh Abdullah to office (A), solidified the supremacy of the Indian Constitution regarding central laws (C), and led to the dissolution of the Plebiscite Front into the National Conference (D).

column6: Consider the following statements about the Kashmir Valley's formation: S1: It is a synclinal basin between the Pir Panjal and Zanskar ranges. S2: It was once a vast lake called "Satisar" according to legend. S3: The Jhelum River drained the lake through the Baramulla gorge. Which are correct?
column14: All three statements are correct. The Kashmir Valley is a synclinal basin, legend describes it as the lake Satisar drained by Kashyapa, and the Jhelum carved the Baramulla gorge to drain the ancient lake.

column6:
Assertion (A): The Karewa formations are economically significant for Kashmir.
Reason (R): They contain the famous saffron fields of Pampore and are rich in fossil remains.

Select the correct code:
column7: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A
column8: Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
column9: A is true but R is false
column10: A is false but R is true
column14: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A. The Karewa tablelands are economically vital as they host the world-famous saffron fields of Pampore and contain rich Pleistocene fossil deposits, explaining their significance.

column6: Which of the following is NOT correct regarding the glaciers of J&K?
column7: Siachen Glacier is the second-longest glacier in the non-polar world
column8: Baltoro Glacier is located entirely within Indian territory
column9: Biafo Glacier feeds the Shigar River in Gilgit-Baltistan
column10: Hispar Glacier connects with Biafo to form an 116 km ice corridor
column14: The Baltoro Glacier is located in Pakistan-occupied Gilgit-Baltistan, not Indian territory. Siachen is the second-longest non-polar glacier, Biafo feeds the Shigar, and Hispar-Biafo form the world's longest glacial corridor outside polar regions.

column6:
Match

List-I (Pass) with

List-II (Elevation/Feature): A. Zoji La - 1. 3,528 metres, connects Srinagar-Leh, B. Fotu La - 2. 4,108 metres, highest on Srinagar-Leh highway, C. Namika La - 3. 3,700 metres, between Lamayuru and Kargil, D. Khardung La - 4. 5,359 metres, gateway to Nubra Valley.

Select the correct code:
column14: Zoji La is at 3,528m connecting Srinagar-Leh, Fotu La at 4,108m is the highest pass on the NH1, Namika La at ~3,700m lies between Lamayuru and Kargil, and Khardung La at 5,359m is the gateway to Nubra Valley.

column6: Consider the following statements about J&K's climatic zones: S1: The Kashmir Valley has a Cfb (temperate oceanic) climate under Köppen classification. S2: Ladakh experiences a BWk (cold desert) climate. S3: Jammu has a Cwa (humid subtropical) climate with dry winters. Which are correct?
column14: All three statements are correct. Kashmir Valley has Cfb (temperate oceanic), Ladakh has BWk (cold desert), and Jammu has Cwa (humid subtropical with dry winters) under Köppen classification.

column6: Which of the following is NOT correct regarding J&K's forest types?
column7: Sub-tropical pine forests are found between 900-1,500 metres in Jammu
column8: Himalayan moist temperate forests occur between 1,500-3,000 metres
column9: Alpine scrub extends beyond 4,500 metres in Ladakh
column10: Sub-alpine forests are dominated by Chir pine in Kashmir
column14: Sub-alpine forests are dominated by Silver Fir (Abies pindrow) and Spruce, not Chir pine. Chir pine (Pinus roxburghii) dominates the lower sub-tropical zones between 900-1,500 metres.

column6:
Assertion (A): The Tulip Garden in Srinagar is Asia's largest.
Reason (R): It is situated on the foothills of the Zabarwan range overlooking Dal Lake.

Select the correct code:
column7: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A
column8: Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
column9: A is true but R is false
column10: A is false but R is true
column14: Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A. The location on Zabarwan foothills overlooking Dal Lake describes its scenic setting but does not explain why it is Asia's largest, which is determined by its area and number of tulip bulbs.

column6:
Match the following: A. Kishtwar High Altitude NP -
1. Only habitat of the Hangul deer, B. Dachigam NP -
2. Markhor and Snow Leopard habitat, C. Hemis NP -
3. Largest NP in India by area, D. Salim Ali NP -
4. Bird sanctuary on Wular Lake periphery.

Select the correct code:
column14: Kishtwar is known for Markhor and Snow Leopard, Dachigam is the only habitat of the Hangul, Hemis is India's largest national park by area, and Salim Ali NP is a bird sanctuary on the periphery of Wular Lake.

column6: Consider the following statements about the Jhelum River: S1: It is a tributary of the Indus River. S2: It enters Pakistan through the Chakothi sector. S3: It has a total length of approximately 725 km. Which are correct?
column14: All three statements are correct. The Jhelum is a tributary of the Indus, enters Pakistan through Chakothi near Uri, and has a total length of approximately 725 km from Verinag to its confluence with the Chenab in Pakistan.

column6: Which of the following is NOT correct?
column7: The Chenab River is called the "Chandrabhaga" in Rigvedic texts
column8: The Ravi River forms the boundary between J&K and Himachal Pradesh
column9: The Tawi River originates from the Kailash Kund glacier in Bhaderwah
column10: The Indus River flows through the Nubra Valley before entering Pakistan
column14: The Ravi River does not form the boundary between J&K and Himachal Pradesh; it flows entirely through Himachal Pradesh and Punjab. The Chenab is called Chandrabhaga in ancient texts, Tawi originates from Kailash Kund, and Indus flows through Nubra.

column6: Consider the following statements about the constitutional mechanism of the Act: S1: The Act was passed under Article 3 of the Constitution. S2: The Presidential Order C.O. 272 preceded the Act. S3: The Act required ratification by half of the state legislatures under Article 368. Which are correct?
column14: S1 and S2 are correct. The Act was passed under Article 3, and C.O. 272 preceded it. S3 is incorrect because state reorganisation under Article 3 does not require ratification by state legislatures under Article 368, which applies only to constitutional amendments.

column6:
Assertion (A): The Reorganisation Act rendered the J&K Constitution inoperative.
Reason (R): Section 4 of the Act explicitly stated that all provisions of the J&K Constitution shall cease to have effect.

Select the correct code:
column7: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A
column8: Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
column9: A is true but R is false
column10: A is false but R is true
column14: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A. Section 4 of the Act explicitly rendered all provisions of the J&K Constitution of 1957 inoperative, thereby removing the special constitutional framework of the erstwhile state.

column6: Which of the following is NOT correct regarding the Act's provisions for the Legislative Assembly?
column7: The Assembly has a 5-year term unless dissolved earlier
column8: The LG can nominate 2 members from the Anglo-Indian community
column9: The quorum for Assembly meetings is 10 members
column10: The Speaker can be removed by a resolution passed by majority of total membership
column14: The 104th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2020 abolished the provision for Anglo-Indian nomination in legislatures. While the Reorganisation Act originally included this, it is no longer operative following the constitutional amendment.

column6:

2. Annual Financial Statement, C. Section 44 -

Select the correct code:
column14: Section 42 deals with the Annual Financial Statement, Section 43 with Money Bills, Section 44 with Supplementary Grants, and Section 45 with Votes on Account and Votes of Credit.

column6: Consider the following statements about the Act's provisions for the High Court: S1: The High Court of J&K and Ladakh continues as a common court. S2: The jurisdiction of the High Court extends to both Union Territories. S3: The Chief Justice is appointed by the President under Article 217. Which are correct?
column14: All three statements are correct. The common High Court for J&K and Ladakh continues, its jurisdiction extends to both UTs, and the Chief Justice is appointed by the President under Article 217 of the Constitution.

column6: Which of the following is NOT correct regarding the Act's adaptation of laws?
column7: 106 central laws were extended to J&K UT
column9: 7 state laws were amended to align with central laws
column10: The Ranbir Penal Code was retained as the criminal code
column14: The Ranbir Penal Code was replaced by the Indian Penal Code (now Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita), not retained. The Act extended 106 central laws, repealed 153 state laws, and amended 7 state laws to align with central legislation.

column6:
Assertion (A): The Reorganisation Act created a separate Public Service Commission for J&K UT.
Reason (R): Section 77 of the Act provides for the composition and functions of the J&K PSC.

Select the correct code:
column7: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A
column8: Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
column9: A is true but R is false
column10: A is false but R is true

column6: Consider the following statements about reported speech: S1: "Say" is used without an indirect object; "tell" requires one. S2: Exclamatory sentences in indirect speech use "exclaimed with joy/sorrow." S3: Universal truths do not change tense in indirect speech. Which are correct?

column6: Consider the following direct-to-indirect conversions: S1: "If I were you, I would accept" → He advised me to accept. S2: "Please, help me" → He requested me to help him. S3: "What are you doing?" → He asked me what I was doing. Which are correct?

column14: All three statements correctly identify conditional sentence types. S1 is Type 1 (real present), S2 is Type 3 (unreal past), and S3 is Type 2 (unreal present). Each follows the standard if-clause and main clause structure for its respective type.
