column6: Consider the following statements about the commencement and structure of the Act: I. The J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019 came into effect on 31st October 2019. II. It reorganized the state into two Union Territories, both having their own separate Legislative Assemblies. Which is correct?
column14: Statement II is false because the Union Territory of Ladakh was created without a legislature, whereas the UT of J&K was created with a legislature.

column6: Consider the following statements regarding the bicameral legislature of the erstwhile state: I. The Act formally abolished the Legislative Council (Upper House) of Jammu and Kashmir. II. All bills pending in the Legislative Council lapsed immediately upon the abolition of the Council. Which is correct?
column14: Under Section 57 of the Act, the Legislative Council was abolished and all bills pending in the Council lapsed on the appointed day.

column6: Consider the following statements regarding the Judiciary under the Act: I. The Act established two separate High Courts for the UT of J&K and the UT of Ladakh. II. The judges of the former High Court of J&K automatically became the judges of the High Court for the new UTs. Which is correct?
column14: Statement I is false. Section 75 states that there shall be a common High Court for both the UT of Jammu and Kashmir and the UT of Ladakh.

column6: Consider the following statements about representation in the Parliament of India: I. The UT of Jammu and Kashmir is allocated 5 seats in the Lok Sabha. II. The UT of Ladakh is allocated 1 seat in the Rajya Sabha. Which is correct?
column14: Statement II is false. Ladakh has 1 seat in the Lok Sabha but 0 seats in the Rajya Sabha. J&K retains 4 seats in the Rajya Sabha.

column6: Consider the following statements regarding the Legislative Assembly seats for Pakistan Occupied Jammu & Kashmir (PoJK): I. 24 seats in the Legislative Assembly of the UT of J&K remain vacant for areas under the occupation of Pakistan. II. These 24 vacant seats are not taken into account for calculating the total membership of the Assembly for government formation. Which is correct?
column14: Under Section 14, 24 seats are reserved for PoJK. They remain vacant and are excluded when calculating the quorum or majority needed to form a government.

column6: Consider the following statements regarding the legislative powers of the J&K Assembly: I. The subjects of 'Police' and 'Public Order' fall under the legislative jurisdiction of the J&K Assembly. II. The subject of 'Land' is completely excluded from the jurisdiction of the J&K Legislative Assembly. Which is correct?
column14: Both are false. Under Section 32, the Assembly can make laws on any matter in the State List EXCEPT "Police" and "Public Order". Unlike Delhi, "Land" remains under the domain of the J&K Assembly.

column6: Consider the following statements regarding the Lieutenant Governor (LG): I. The Lieutenant Governor of the UT of J&K is appointed by the President of India. II. The LG has the power to promulgate ordinances during the recess of the Legislative Assembly. Which is correct?
column14: Both statements are true. The President appoints the LG (Article 239) and Section 52 of the Act grants the LG ordinance-making powers when the assembly is not in session.

column6: Consider the following statements regarding the application of laws: I. According to the Act, all Central Laws listed in the Fifth Schedule were made applicable to the UTs of J&K and Ladakh. II. The Indian Penal Code (IPC) officially replaced the Ranbir Penal Code (RPC). Which is correct?
column14: The Fifth Schedule of the Act made over 100 central laws explicitly applicable, and formally repealed state-specific laws like the RPC, replacing it with the IPC.

column6: Consider the following statements regarding political reservations: I. The Act provides for the reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes (SC) and Scheduled Tribes (ST) in the Legislative Assembly of J&K. II. The reservation of these seats is strictly based on the proportion of their population to the total population of the UT. Which is correct?
column14: Under Section 14(6), seats are reserved for SCs and STs, and the number bears the same proportion to total seats as their population bears to the total population of the UT.

column6: Consider the following statements regarding the division of assets and liabilities: I. The Act mandated the Central Government to appoint Advisory Committees for the apportionment of assets, rights, and liabilities. II. These committees were tasked with managing disputes over assets strictly between the newly formed UT of Ladakh and the neighboring state of Himachal Pradesh. Which is correct?
column14: Statement II is false. The Advisory Committees (Sections 84 and 85) were appointed to apportion the assets and liabilities of the former State of J&K between the two new UTs (J&K and Ladakh), not with Himachal Pradesh.

column6: Consider the following statements regarding motion: I. A body can have constant speed but varying velocity. II. A body can have constant velocity but varying speed. Which is correct?
column14: Statement I is True: Uniform circular motion has constant speed but changing direction, so velocity changes. Statement II is False: If velocity is constant, both speed and direction MUST be constant.

column6: Consider the following statements about forces and motion: I. An object momentarily at rest can have non-zero acceleration. II. An object in uniform straight-line motion has zero acceleration. Which is correct?
column14: Statement I is True: A ball thrown straight up is momentarily at rest at its peak but still has an acceleration of 9.8 m/s² downwards. Statement II is True: Uniform motion means velocity isn't changing, hence 0 acceleration.

column6: Consider the following statements regarding Newton’s Laws: I. Inertia is the internal force that keeps an object in motion. II. A constant net force is required to keep an object moving at a constant velocity in a vacuum. Which is correct?
column14: Statement I is False: Inertia is a property of matter, not a force. Statement II is False: According to the 1st Law, NO net force is needed to maintain a constant velocity.

column6: Consider the following statements about Newton’s Third Law: I. Action and reaction forces always act on the exact same object. II. Because action and reaction are equal and opposite, they cancel each other out. Which is correct?
column14: Statement I is False: They act on two different interacting objects. Statement II is False: Because they act on different objects, they do NOT cancel each other out.

column6: Consider the following statements about Mass and Weight: I. Mass is a scalar quantity, while weight is a vector quantity. II. The weight of an object becomes absolute zero in a state of free fall. Which is correct?
column14: Statement I is True: Weight is a force pointing downward. Statement II is True: In free fall, you experience weightlessness or zero apparent weight because there is no normal force pushing back up against you.

column6: Consider the following statements about electric flow: I. Conventional current flows from the negative terminal to the positive terminal. II. Electrons flow from a region of lower potential to a region of higher potential. Which is correct?
column14: Statement I is False: Conventional current flows Positive to Negative. Statement II is True: Electrons are negatively charged, so they are repelled by negative/lower potential and attracted to positive/higher potential.

column6: Consider the following statements about electrical units: I. The Kilowatt-hour (kWh) is a standard unit of electrical power. II. One Kilowatt-hour is exactly equal to 3.6 million Joules. Which is correct?
column14: Statement I is False: Kilowatt-hour is a unit of Energy, not Power. Power is measured in Watts/Kilowatts. Statement II is True.

column6: Consider the following statements about circuit components: I. An ammeter must always be connected in parallel within a circuit. II. A voltmeter is designed to have very low electrical resistance. Which is correct?
column14: Both are completely swapped. Ammeters are connected in series and have low resistance. Voltmeters are connected in parallel and have high resistance.

column6: Consider the following statements based on Ohm's Law and Power (assuming resistance is constant): I. Doubling the voltage across a resistor will perfectly double the power consumed. II. Electrical energy is calculated by dividing Power by time (E = P/t). Which is correct?
column14: Statement I is False: Power = V²/R. If you double the voltage, the power quadruples. Statement II is False: Energy = Power × time, not Power divided by time.

column6: Consider the following statements about voltage and current: I. Voltage is defined as the rate of flow of electric charge. II. Current will only flow if there is a potential difference (voltage) between two points. Which is correct?
column14: Statement I is False: Current is the rate of flow of charge. Voltage is the work done to move a charge. Statement II is True: Voltage provides the push required for current to flow.

column6: Consider the following statements about architecture: I. RISC architectures use variable-length instructions to save memory. II. A data hazard occurs when two pipelined instructions need the same hardware resource. Which is correct?
column14: RISC uses fixed-length instructions. A clash over hardware is a structural hazard, not a data hazard.

column6: Consider the following statements regarding memory: I. Level 1 cache is split for instructions and data. II. A write-through cache policy reduces system bus traffic compared to a write-back policy. Which is correct?
column14: Level 1 is split while Level 1 is unified. Write-through increases bus traffic by writing to RAM immediately.

column6: Consider the following statements about storage: I. In solid state drives, writing to an empty page is faster than erasing a block. II. Wear leveling is used in magnetic hard disk drives to prevent platter degradation. Which is correct?
column14: Solid state drives erase data in slow blocks. Wear leveling applies only to flash memory cells, not magnetic platters.

column6: Consider the following statements regarding buses: I. Peripheral Component Interconnect Express uses parallel data transmission for high bandwidth. II. The Northbridge chipset handled high-speed communication between the processor and memory. Which is correct?
column14: PCIe uses high-speed serial lanes, not parallel. The Northbridge handled fast components like memory and graphics.

column6: Consider the following statements about memory management: I. Static RAM requires periodic electrical refreshing to retain data. II. The memory management unit translates physical addresses into virtual addresses. Which is correct?
column14: Dynamic RAM requires refreshing, not Static RAM. The management unit translates virtual addresses into physical addresses, not the reverse.

column6: Consider the following statements about data transfers: I. Direct memory access lets hardware access system memory independently of the processor. II. The processor is completely halted and cannot execute instructions during a direct memory access transfer. Which is correct?
column14: Direct memory access handles data transfers independently. The processor can still execute instructions from its cache during this time.

column6: Consider the following statements about the boot process: I. Unified Extensible Firmware Interface supports booting from drives larger than two terabytes. II. The master boot record is permanently stored on a read-only memory chip on the motherboard. Which is correct?
column14: UEFI fixes the two terabyte limit of legacy systems. The master boot record is stored on the storage drive itself, not the motherboard.

column6: Consider the following statements regarding logic systems: I. The NAND gate is a universal gate capable of implementing any boolean function. II. The twos complement binary system has two different representations for the number zero. Which is correct?
column14: NAND is a universal gate. Twos complement was adopted specifically because it has only one representation for zero.

column6: Consider the following statements about system input output: I. A non-maskable interrupt can be ignored if the processor is running a high-priority kernel task. II. Polling consumes more processor cycles than an interrupt-driven input output system. Which is correct?
column14: Non-maskable interrupts signal fatal hardware errors and can never be ignored. Polling wastes processor cycles by constantly checking hardware status.

column6: Consider the following statements about computing architectures: I. The Von Neumann architecture uses separate memory spaces and buses for instructions and data. II. The Harvard architecture allows the processor to fetch instructions and read data simultaneously. Which is correct?
column14: Von Neumann uses a unified memory space and shared bus. Harvard uses separate buses, allowing simultaneous fetching and reading.

column6: A DC voltage source of 100 V is applied to a series circuit comprising a 10 Ω resistor and a non-linear load whose V-I characteristic is given by V=5I² (where I>0). Determine the steady-state current I flowing through the circuit.
column14: Apply KVL to the series loop: 100 = 10I + V_load. Substitute the non-linear characteristic: 100 = 10I + 5I². Dividing by 5 gives the quadratic equation I² + 2I - 20 = 0. Solving for positive current: I = (-2 + √(4 - 4(1)(-20)))/2 = (-2 + √84)/2 = -1 + √21 ≈ 3.58 A.

column6: In a given network, Node A is connected to a 24 V independent voltage source via a 2 Ω resistor. Node A is also connected to Node B via a 4 Ω resistor. Node B is connected to ground via a 2 Ω resistor. A voltage-dependent current source of magnitude 0.5(V_A) flows from ground directly into Node B. Using nodal analysis, calculate the voltage V_B.
column14: Apply KCL at Node B: (V_B - V_A)/4 + V_B/2 - 0.5(V_A) = 0. Multiplying by 4 yields: V_B - V_A + 2V_B - 2V_A = 0 => 3V_B = 3V_A => V_B = V_A. Apply KCL at Node A: (V_A - 24)/2 + (V_A - V_B)/4 = 0. Multiplying by 4 yields: 2V_A - 48 + V_A - V_B = 0. Substitute V_A = V_B: 2V_B - 48 + V_B - V_B = 0 => 2V_B = 48 => V_B = 24 V.

column6: The nodal admittance matrix of a passive, resistive 2-node circuit (excluding the reference ground) is given by Y = [[4, -1], [-1, 3]] S. What is the Thevenin equivalent resistance R_th looking into Node 1 with respect to ground?
column14: The admittance matrix equation is [Y][V] = [I]. To find the Thevenin resistance looking into Node 1, we inject a 1 A test current into Node 1 (I_1 = 1, I_2 = 0) and find V_1. The equations are: 4V_1 - V_2 = 1 and -V_1 + 3V_2 = 0 => V_1 = 3V_2. Substitute into the first: 4(3V_2) - V_2 = 1 => 11V_2 = 1 => V_2 = 1/11 V. Therefore, V_1 = 3/11 V. R_th = V_1 / 1 A = 3/11 Ω.

column6: An AC source with an internal impedance of Z_s = (3+j4) Ω is connected to a variable load impedance Z_L. If the source voltage is 10 V (RMS), what is the maximum average power that can be transferred to the load?
column14: For maximum power transfer in an AC circuit, the load impedance must be the complex conjugate of the source impedance: Z_L = Z_s* = (3 - j4) Ω. The total circuit impedance is Z_total = (3 + j4) + (3 - j4) = 6 Ω. The RMS current is I = V / Z_total = 10 / 6 = 5/3 A. The maximum power is P_max = I² × R_L = (5/3)² × 3 = (25/9) × 3 = 25/3 ≈ 8.33 W.

column6: A linear bilateral DC network contains two independent voltage sources, V_1 and V_2. When V_1 = 10 V and V_2 = 0 V, the current I flowing through a 5 Ω resistor is measured as 2 A (from node X to Y). When V_1 = 0 V and V_2 = 20 V, the current is 4 A (from node X to Y). If V_1 = 20 V and V_2 = -10 V are applied simultaneously, what is the power dissipated in the 5 Ω resistor?
column14: Using Superposition, the current is a linear combination of the sources: I = (k_1 × V_1) + (k_2 × V_2). From Case 1: 2 = k_1 × 10 => k_1 = 0.2. From Case 2: 4 = k_2 × 20 => k_2 = 0.2. For the new condition: I_new = 0.2(20) + 0.2(-10) = 4 - 2 = 2 A. The power dissipated is P = I_new² × R = 2² × 5 = 20 W.

column6: A practical DC voltage source has an internal resistance of R_in = 2 Ω. What load resistance R_L must be connected across its terminals to achieve exactly an 80% power transfer efficiency from the source to the load?
column14: Power transfer efficiency is defined as η = P_load / P_total = (I² × R_L) / (I² × (R_L + R_in)) = R_L / (R_L + 2). Set this to 80% (0.8): 0.8 = R_L / (R_L + 2). Solving yields 0.8(R_L) + 1.6 = R_L => 0.2(R_L) = 1.6 => R_L = 8 Ω.

column6: A series RLC circuit is designed with R = 10 Ω, L = 10 mH, and C = 1 µF. Determine the Quality factor (Q) and the Bandwidth (BW) of the circuit.
column14: For a series RLC circuit, BW = R/L = 10 / (10 × 10⁻³) = 1000 rad/s. Resonant frequency ω_0 = 1/√(LC) = 1/√(10 × 10⁻³ × 1 × 10⁻⁶) = 10000 rad/s. Quality factor Q = ω_0 / BW = 10000 / 1000 = 10.

column6: In a parallel RLC circuit, the resonant frequency is 1000 rad/s and the -3 dB bandwidth is 100 rad/s. If the value of the capacitance is exactly 10 µF, calculate the value of the resistance R present in the circuit.
column14: For a parallel RLC circuit, the bandwidth in rad/s is given by BW = 1 / (RC). Given BW = 100 rad/s and C = 10 µF = 10 × 10⁻⁶ F, we have 100 = 1 / (R × 10⁻⁵) => R = 1 / (100 × 10⁻⁵) = 1 / (10⁻³) = 1000 Ω.

column6: The voltage transfer function of a first-order filter is given by H(s) = 10s / (s + 100). What type of filter does this represent, and what is its maximum gain in decibels (dB)?
column14: Evaluate H(s) at extremes. At DC (s -> 0), H(0) = 0. At high frequencies (s -> ∞), H(∞) -> 10s / s = 10. Because it blocks low frequencies and passes high frequencies, it is a High-Pass Filter. The maximum linear gain is 10. Converting to decibels: 20 × log10(10) = 20(1) = 20 dB.

column6: A simple RC low-pass filter has a cutoff frequency of 1 kHz. If the physical values of both the resistor and the capacitor are doubled, what will be the new -3 dB cutoff frequency of the filter?
column14: The cutoff frequency of an RC low-pass filter is f_c = 1 / (2πRC) = 1 kHz. If the new values are R' = 2R and C' = 2C, the new cutoff frequency is f_c' = 1 / (2π(2R)(2C)) = (1/4) × (1 / 2πRC) = (1/4) × 1 kHz = 250 Hz.

column6: Consider the following statements regarding the Union Budget: I. Revenue receipts include both tax and non-tax revenues of the government. II. Disinvestment of government equity in Public Sector Enterprises is classified as a revenue receipt. Which of the statements given above is correct?
column14: Statement I is correct. Statement II is false because disinvestment involves the sale of assets, meaning it is strictly classified as a Capital Receipt, not a Revenue Receipt.

column6: Consider the following statements about Fiscal Deficit: I. It reflects the total borrowing requirement of the government from all external and internal sources. II. A higher fiscal deficit necessarily leads to higher national inflation in all economic conditions. Which of the statements given above is correct?
column14: Statement I is correct as fiscal deficit is the exact measure of total borrowings. Statement II is false because if the borrowed money is used for productive capital asset creation, it may not cause inflation and can instead boost growth.

column6: Consider the following statements regarding the Ayushman Bharat scheme: I. It provides a health insurance cover of five lakh rupees per individual per year for secondary and tertiary care. II. There is no cap on family size or the age of family members under the scheme. Which of the statements given above is correct?
column14: Statement I is false because the cover of five lakh rupees is provided per family per year, not per individual. Statement II is true, as removing caps ensures vulnerable members like the elderly are covered.

column6: Consider the following statements regarding the Jal Jeevan Mission: I. It aims to provide functional household tap connections to every rural household by the year 2030. II. The funding pattern is a 50-50 ratio between the Centre and States for Himalayan and North-Eastern States. Which of the statements given above is correct?
column14: Both statements are false. The target year for providing functional household tap connections is 2024, not 2030. For Himalayan and North-Eastern States, the funding ratio is 90:10, not 50:50.

column6: Consider the following statements regarding the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act: I. The Act completely prohibits the Central Government from borrowing any funds from the Reserve Bank of India. II. The Act contains an escape clause allowing deviation from the fiscal deficit target in times of national calamity. Which of the statements given above is correct?
column14: Statement I is false because temporary borrowing is allowed through Ways and Means Advances. Statement II is true, as the escape clause was famously utilized during the COVID pandemic to manage the fiscal shock.

column6: Consider the following statements regarding the electronic National Agriculture Market: I. It completely replaces the existing physical agricultural produce market committees across the participating states. II. The scheme is implemented by the Small Farmers Agribusiness Consortium. Which of the statements given above is correct?
column14: Statement I is false because e-NAM does not replace physical mandis; instead, it networks existing physical mandis into a unified national electronic market. Statement II is true.

column6: Consider the following statements regarding the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana: I. It provides a life insurance cover of two lakh rupees payable upon the natural death of the account holder. II. The scheme offers an overdraft facility of up to ten thousand rupees to eligible account holders. Which of the statements given above is correct?
column14: Statement I is false because the two lakh rupee cover is strictly for accidental death, not natural death. Statement II is true, providing emergency liquidity to vulnerable account holders.

column6: Consider the following statements regarding tax revenues in the Union Budget: I. The collection from Income Tax has consistently exceeded Corporate Tax in the last two Union Budgets. II. Revenue collected from cesses forms a permanent part of the divisible pool of taxes shared with states. Which of the statements given above is correct?
column14: Statement I is true as personal income tax collections have recently overtaken corporate tax. Statement II is false because Article 270 strictly excludes cesses and surcharges from the divisible pool shared with state governments.

column6: Consider the following statements regarding banking sector reforms: I. The Indradhanush framework was launched specifically to recapitalize and reform private sector banks. II. The Prompt Corrective Action framework restricts weak banks from issuing dividends and expanding branches. Which of the statements given above is correct?
column14: Statement I is false because the Indradhanush framework was specifically formulated to revamp Public Sector Banks, not private ones. Statement II is true regarding the restrictions placed under PCA.

column6: Consider the following statements regarding the Stand Up India Scheme: I. It facilitates bank loans strictly for setting up greenfield enterprises. II. The scheme mandates every bank branch to support at least one woman entrepreneur and one Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe borrower. Which of the statements given above is correct?
column14: Both statements are correct. The scheme explicitly targets greenfield first-time ventures and mandates inclusive lending quotas per bank branch to promote grassroots entrepreneurship among marginalized groups.

column6: Calculate the Harmonic Mean of the numbers 2, 4, and 8.
column14: Harmonic Mean = n / (∑(1/x)). Here n = 3. The sum of reciprocals is 1/2 + 1/4 + 1/8 = 4/8 + 2/8 + 1/8 = 7/8. So, HM = 3 / (7/8) = 24 / 7 ≈ 3.43.

column6: The mean weight of 15 students is 40 kg. If one more student joins the class, the mean weight increases by 2 kg. What is the exact weight of the new student?
column14: The total weight of the 15 students is 15 × 40 = 600 kg. With the new student, the total students are 16 and the new mean is 42 kg. The new total weight is 16 × 42 = 672 kg. Therefore, the weight of the new student is 672 - 600 = 72 kg.

column6: Which measure of central tendency is uniquely determined by the graphical intersection of the 'less than' and 'more than' ogive curves?
column14: An ogive is a cumulative frequency polygon. The point where the 'less than' ogive and 'more than' ogive intersect corresponds exactly to the Median of the distribution on the x-axis.

column6: Consider the following statements regarding the mode: I. The mode is the only measure of central tendency that is appropriate to use for nominal (categorical) data. II. In a perfectly symmetrical bell-shaped distribution, the mean, median, and mode are all equal. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
column14: Statement I is true; for data like "eye color" or "brands", you can only find the most frequent item (mode). Statement II is a fundamental property of a perfectly symmetrical (normal) distribution.

column6: If the arithmetic mean of 14 observations is 25, and the arithmetic mean of another 16 observations is 35, what is the combined arithmetic mean of all 30 observations?
column14: The formula for combined mean is (n1x1 + n2x2) / (n1 + n2). Here, it is (14 × 25 + 16 × 35) / 30 = (350 + 560) / 30 = 910 / 30 ≈ 30.33.

column6: If a variable x takes the values 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5 with corresponding frequencies 5, 4, 3, 2, and 1, what is the arithmetic mean of the distribution?

Consider the following statements about quartiles and partitions: I. The First Quartile (Q1) represents the 25th percentile of the data. II. The Interquartile Range contains exactly the middle 50 percent of the observations in a dataset. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
column14: Both statements are correct. Q1 cuts off the lowest 25% of the data. The Interquartile Range is calculated as Q3 - Q1, which spans exactly the middle 50% of the dataset.

column6: In a moderately asymmetrical distribution, the Mode is given as 32 and the Arithmetic Mean is 35. Find the value of the Median using the empirical relationship.
column14: The empirical formula is Mode = 3(Median) - 2(Mean). Substituting the values: 32 = 3(Median) - 2(35) => 32 = 3(Median) - 70 => 3(Median) = 102 => Median = 34.

column6: For a dataset containing the values {10, -10, 20, -20}, which of the following measures of central tendency mathematically cannot be calculated?
column14: The Geometric Mean involves taking the nth root of the product of all observations. It is mathematically undefined and cannot be calculated for datasets that contain negative values.

column6: Consider the following statements regarding the Harmonic Mean (HM): I. The harmonic mean is defined as the reciprocal of the arithmetic mean of the reciprocals of the observations. II. The harmonic mean gives the highest weight to the largest items in a dataset. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
column14: Statement I is the exact mathematical definition of the Harmonic Mean. Statement II is false because the Harmonic Mean gives the highest weight to the smallest items and the lowest weight to the largest items.

column6: An AM transmitter radiates 54 kW at 100 percent modulation. What is the total power radiated if the carrier is unmodulated?
column14: The formula for total AM power is Pt = Pc times 1 plus square of modulation index divided by 2. Given Pt = 54 kW and index = 1, we get 54 = 1.5 Pc. Thus Pc = 36 kW.

column6: A phase modulated signal has a maximum phase deviation of 2 radians. If the modulating frequency is doubled while keeping amplitude constant, what is the new maximum phase deviation?
column14: In phase modulation, phase deviation depends only on the amplitude of the modulating signal. Changing frequency has no effect on phase deviation.

column6: A signal is the mathematical product of 10 cos 200πt and cos 800πt. What is the minimum Nyquist sampling rate in Hertz?
column14: Using trigonometric identities, the signal expands to 5 times the sum of cos 1000πt and cos 600πt. The maximum frequency is 500 Hz. The Nyquist rate is twice this frequency, equaling 1000 Hz.

column6: A carrier is frequency modulated by a 10 kHz sine wave resulting in a modulation index of 5. What is the approximate transmission bandwidth using Carsons rule?
column14: Frequency deviation is 50 kHz. Carsons rule states bandwidth is twice the sum of frequency deviation and modulating frequency. This equals 120 kHz.

column6: A voice signal band-limited to 3.4 kHz is sampled at 8 kHz and encoded into PCM with 256 quantization levels. What is the minimum baseband transmission bandwidth?
column14: 256 levels require 8 bits per sample. The bit rate is 8 times 8 kHz, equaling 64 kbps. Minimum baseband bandwidth is half the bit rate, which is 32 kHz.

column6: What is the minimum frequency separation required for two orthogonal signals in non-coherent FSK if the symbol rate is Rs?
column14: For FSK signals to be orthogonal, minimum frequency separation is half the symbol rate for coherent detection, but exactly the symbol rate for non-coherent detection.

column6: Consider these statements on delta modulation: I. Slope overload occurs when the signal changes rapidly. II. Granular noise is reduced by increasing step size. Which is correct?
column14: Statement I is true as slope overload happens when the analog signal rises faster than the staircase can track. Statement II is false as granular noise is reduced by decreasing the step size.

column6: Consider these statements on digital modulation: I. Offset QPSK prevents 180 degree phase transitions. II. QPSK needs half the bandwidth of BPSK. Which is correct?
column14: Both are true. Offset QPSK delays one stream to prevent simultaneous switching. QPSK transmits 2 bits per symbol, effectively halving bandwidth compared to BPSK.

column6: Consider these statements on analog receivers: I. Synchronous detectors are immune to the threshold effect. II. The figure of merit for a single sideband receiver is one. Which is correct?
column14: Both are true. Synchronous detectors do not suffer from the threshold effect at low signal to noise ratios. The figure of merit for a single sideband receiver is 1.

column6: Consider these statements on quantization: I. Uniform quantization gives better signal ratios for weak signals. II. Companding maintains constant ratios across all levels. Which is correct?
column14: Statement I is false because uniform quantization gives poor ratios for weak signals due to large step sizes. Statement II is true as this is the exact purpose of companding.

column6: Consider these statements on carbon markets: I. The concept of carbon trading was formally introduced globally by the Kyoto Protocol. II. One carbon credit is exactly equivalent to one metric ton of carbon dioxide removed or avoided. Which is correct?
column14: Both statements are true. Carbon trading originated with the Kyoto Protocol, and the standard unit of one credit always equals one metric ton of carbon dioxide equivalent.

column6: Which of the following statements regarding Indian disaster administration is not correct?
column7: The Prime Minister is the ex officio chairperson of the National Disaster Management Authority.
column8: The National Executive Committee is chaired by the Union Home Minister.
column9: State Disaster Management Authorities are headed by respective Chief Ministers.
column10: District Disaster Management Authorities are co-chaired by elected local body representatives.
column14: The statement in option B is incorrect because the National Executive Committee is actually chaired by the Union Home Secretary, not the Home Minister.

column6: Consider these statements on the International Solar Alliance: I. Membership is strictly restricted to countries located partially or fully between the Tropics. II. It is the first international intergovernmental treaty-based organization headquartered in India. Which is correct?
column14: Statement I is false because membership is now open to all member states of the United Nations regardless of their geographic location. Statement II is true.

column6: Consider these statements on climate finance: I. The Green Climate Fund was established during the Earth Summit in Rio de Janeiro in 1992. II. The World Bank currently serves as the permanent trustee of the Green Climate Fund. Which is correct?
column14: Statement I is false as the Green Climate Fund was established much later at the 2010 climate conference in Cancun. Statement II is true.

column6: Which of the following statements regarding the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure is not correct?
column7: Its secretariat is permanently located in New Delhi.
column8: It was officially launched by the United Nations Environment Programme.
column9: It aims to promote the resilience of new and existing infrastructure systems.
column10: It acts as a partnership of national governments and UN agencies.
column14: The statement in option B is incorrect because the coalition was officially launched by the Prime Minister of India, not the United Nations.

column6: Consider these statements on Indias climate action plan: I. The National Water Mission is one of the eight core missions under the National Action Plan on Climate Change. II. The National Mission for a Green India focuses exclusively on expanding monoculture commercial timber plantations. Which is correct?
column14: Statement I is true. Statement II is false because the Green India Mission focuses on enhancing biodiversity and restoring degraded ecosystems, not just planting commercial monoculture timber for profit.

column6: Which of the following statements regarding the Sendai Framework is not correct?
column7: It succeeded the Hyogo Framework for Action.
column8: It is a voluntary agreement on disaster risk reduction.
column9: It is a legally binding international treaty on member nations.
column10: It aims to substantially reduce global disaster mortality.
column14: The statement in option C is incorrect because the Sendai Framework is a voluntary, non-binding agreement. The other three statements are completely true.

column6: Consider these statements on disaster notification in India: I. Heatwaves and lightning are officially classified as notified national disasters under the central act. II. State governments can use up to 10 percent of their disaster response fund for local unnotified disasters. Which is correct?
column14: Statement I is false because heatwaves and lightning are not notified national disasters; states manage them locally. Statement II is true as states are granted this 10 percent flexibility rule.

column6: Which of the following statements regarding the Paris Agreement is not correct?
column7: It aims to limit global warming to well below 2 degrees Celsius.
column8: Nationally Determined Contributions are strictly legally binding on all member nations.
column9: It operates on a five year cycle of increasingly ambitious climate action.
column10: It is an international treaty under the United Nations climate framework.
column14: The statement in option B is incorrect. While submitting the contributions is mandatory, the specific emission reduction targets inside them are voluntary and not legally binding.

column6: Consider these statements on early warning systems: I. The Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services is responsible for issuing tsunami early warnings. II. The SAFAR initiative provides early warnings exclusively for sudden geological disasters like earthquakes. Which is correct?
column14: Statement I is true. Statement II is false because SAFAR stands for System of Air Quality and Weather Forecasting and Research, and it exclusively monitors air pollution and weather, not earthquakes.

column6: Consider these statements on Indias three stage nuclear program: I. The second stage utilizes fast breeder reactors. II. Plutonium 239 is the primary fuel used in the third stage. Which is correct?
column14: Third stage uses Thorium, not Plutonium 239. Stage 2 uses fast breeder reactors.

column6: Which of the following statements regarding Directive Principles of State Policy is not correct?
column7: They are fundamental in the governance of the country.
column8: They can override Fundamental Rights in certain specific cases.
column9: They are automatically enforced by subordinate courts.
column10: They require legislative action for implementation.
column14: DPSPs are non justiciable and cannot be automatically enforced by courts.

column6: Consider these statements on the Aditya L1 space mission: I. It will be placed in a geostationary orbit around Earth. II. It is designed to observe the solar corona and photosphere. Which is correct?
column14: Aditya L1 is placed in a halo orbit around Lagrange Point 1, not a geostationary orbit.

column6: Consider these statements on the Preamble of the Indian Constitution: I. The word secular was added by the 44th Amendment Act. II. The Supreme Court considers it an integral part of the Constitution. Which is correct?
column14: Secular was added by the 42nd Amendment, not the 44th. The Preamble is part of the constitution.

column6: Consider these statements on the PM KISAN scheme: I. It provides monetary support exclusively to small and marginal farmers. II. It is a central sector scheme completely funded by the Central Government. Which is correct?
column14: Initially for small or marginal farmers, but later expanded to ALL landholding farmers, making statement I false. It is 100 percent centrally funded.

column6: Consider these statements on the Agni V missile system: I. It is a submarine launched ballistic missile. II. It features Multiple Independently Targetable Reentry Vehicle technology. Which is correct?
column14: Agni V is a land based ICBM, not submarine launched. It does feature MIRV technology.

column6: Consider these statements on Indian disaster response: I. The National Disaster Response Force functions under the Ministry of Defense. II. State governments fully fund their respective State Disaster Response Funds. Which is correct?
column14: NDRF falls under the Ministry of Home Affairs. SDRF is jointly funded 75 to 25 or 90 to 10 by Centre and State.

column6: Which of the following statements regarding the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code is not correct?
column7: It establishes time bound processes for insolvency resolution.
column8: The adjudicating authority for corporate persons is the Debt Recovery Tribunal.
column9: Financial creditors entirely form the committee of creditors.
column10: It aims to maximize the value of assets of corporate debtors.
column14: The adjudicating authority for corporate persons is the National Company Law Tribunal. DRT is for individuals.

column6: Consider these statements on the BRICS grouping: I. The New Development Bank was established by the BRICS member states. II. Argentina officially joined the group as a full member in 2024. Which is correct?
column14: Argentina formally declined the invitation to join BRICS in early 2024.

column6: Consider these statements on global climate initiatives: I. The Loss and Damage Fund was officially operationalized at COP28. II. India has formally committed to achieving net zero emissions by 2050. Which is correct?
column14: India committed to net zero by 2070, not 2050. The Loss and Damage fund was launched at COP28.

column6: Consider these statements on the JK Reorganisation Act 2019: I. The Legislative Assembly can make laws concerning police and public order. II. The Lieutenant Governor has the power to promulgate ordinances. Which is correct?
column14: The JK Legislative Assembly cannot make laws on police and public order as they remain with the Centre.

column8: Karewa soils are highly suitable for saffron cultivation.
column9: Wular lake is a tectonic lake formed by faulting.

column6: Consider these statements on JK history: I. The Treaty of Amritsar was signed in the year 1846. II. Maharaja Gulab Singh purchased Kashmir from the British East India Company. Which is correct?
column14: Both statements are historically correct regarding the formation of the Dogra dynasty.

column6: Consider these statements on JK flora and fauna: I. The Hangul is the state animal of the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir. II. Dachigam National Park is located in the Pir Panjal mountain range. Which is correct?
column14: Hangul is the state animal, but Dachigam is in the Zabarwan range, not Pir Panjal.

column6: Which of the following statements regarding the JK Reorganisation Act 2019 is not correct?

column8: It created two separate high courts for the two new Union Territories.
column9: Four sitting members of the Rajya Sabha were retained for the UT of JK.

column14: The Act retained a common High Court for both the UT of JK and the UT of Ladakh.

column6: Select the grammatically correct sentence:
column7: Neither the manager nor the employees was aware of the new policy.
column8: Neither the manager nor the employees were aware of the new policy.
column9: Neither the manager or the employees were aware of the new policy.
column10: Neither the manager nor the employees is aware of the new policy.
column14: Rule of proximity states the verb agrees with the subject closest to it, which is the plural employees.

column6: Choose the correct passive voice for the sentence: Who tore this beautiful document?
column7: By whom this beautiful document was torn?
column8: By whom was this beautiful document torn?
column9: Who was torn by this beautiful document?
column10: By who was this beautiful document torn?
column14: In interrogative sentences, the auxiliary verb comes before the subject in passive voice.

column6: Which of the following statements regarding official email etiquette is not correct?
column7: The blind carbon copy field is used to keep recipients hidden from each other.
column8: Writing in all capital letters indicates urgency and is highly recommended.
column9: The subject line should concisely reflect the main purpose of the email.
column10: Official drafting requires a formal tone completely free from slang.
column14: Writing in all caps is considered shouting in email etiquette and is highly discouraged.

column6: Choose the correct indirect speech for: He said to me Do not cross the restricted border.
column7: He said to me to not cross the restricted border.
column8: He forbade me to cross the restricted border.
column9: He requested me to not cross the restricted border.
column10: He ordered me that I should not cross the restricted border.
column14: The verb forbade inherently contains a negative meaning, so not is removed in the indirect speech.

column6: What is the meaning of the idiom To play devils advocate?
column7: To secretly plot against a legitimate organization.
column8: To present a counter argument just to test the strength of an opposing view.
column9: To blindly defend a criminal in a court of law.
column10: To purposefully create chaos in a peaceful situation.
column14: Playing devils advocate means arguing against a point just to spur debate or test its validity.

column6: Statements: Only a few tigers are lions. All lions are animals. Conclusions: I. All tigers being animals is a possibility. II. All tigers being lions is a possibility.
column14: Only a few tigers are lions means some are, and some are definitely NOT. Therefore, all tigers can never be lions. However, there is no restriction preventing all tigers from being animals.

column6: If A plus B means A is the brother of B. A minus B means A is the sister of B. A times B means A is the father of B. Which of the following equations means P is the aunt of Q?
column14: P minus R means P is the sister of R. R times Q means R is the father of Q. Therefore, P is the paternal aunt of Q.

column6: Find the next number in the series: 2, 3, 10, 39, 172, ?
column14: Logic is multiplied by 1 plus 1 squared, multiplied by 2 plus 2 squared, multiplied by 3 plus 3 squared. Thus 172 multiplied by 5 plus 25 equals 885.

column6: In a class of 100 students, 60 passed in English, 50 passed in Mathematics, and 20 passed in neither subject. How many students passed in exactly one subject?
column14: Total is 100. 20 passed neither, so 80 passed at least one. English plus Math minus Both equals 80. 60 plus 50 minus Both equals 80, meaning Both equals 30. Only English is 30, Only Math is 20. Total exactly one equals 50.

column6: Select the related word pair: Symphony : Composer
column14: A composer creates a symphony. A painter creates a fresco.

column6: A train crosses a stationary pole in 15 seconds and a 300 meter long platform in 25 seconds. What is the speed of the train?
column14: Speed equals Length divided by 15. Speed also equals Length plus 300 divided by 25. Solving gives Length equals 450. Speed is 450 divided by 15 equals 30.

column6: A dishonest dealer professes to sell his goods at cost price but uses a false weight of 800 grams for a kilogram. What is his actual profit percentage?
column14: He gains 200 grams on an investment of 800 grams. Profit percent is 200 divided by 800 multiplied by 100 equals 25 percent.

column6: The difference between compound interest and simple interest on a certain sum at 10 percent per annum for exactly 3 years is 93 rupees. What is the principal sum?
column14: Difference for 3 years is P multiplied by square of rate/100 multiplied by 3 plus rate/100. Solving gives P equals 3000.

column6: The average age of a class of 40 students is 15 years. When the age of the teacher is included, the average increases by 1 year. What is the exact age of the teacher?
column14: Total age of 40 students is 600. Total age of 41 people is 41 multiplied by 16 equals 656. The difference is 56.

column6: Consider a dataset with an arithmetic mean of 12. If every single observation is multiplied by 2 and then 3 is added to it, what will be the new arithmetic mean?
column14: If all observations are multiplied by a constant and added to, the mean undergoes the exact same mathematical operations. 12 multiplied by 2 plus 3 equals 27.

column6: Consider these statements regarding constitutional writs: I. The writ of Prohibition is issued only against judicial and quasi judicial authorities. II. A writ of Certiorari can be issued against administrative authorities affecting individual rights. Which is correct?
column14: Both statements are true. Prohibition is strictly for judicial and quasi judicial bodies. Post 1970 rulings by the Supreme Court expanded Certiorari to cover administrative authorities affecting individual rights.

column6: Consider these statements regarding defence and space technology: I. The NAVIC satellite navigation system utilizes twenty four geostationary satellites. II. A ramjet engine requires forward motion to produce thrust and has no moving parts. Which is correct?
column14: Statement I is false because NAVIC relies on a constellation of only 7 or 8 satellites, not 24. Statement II is true as ramjets compress incoming air using the forward speed of the vehicle.

column6: Consider these statements regarding the Union Budget: I. The Monetised Deficit represents the total borrowings of the government from the open market. II. Capital receipts always lead to the creation of a liability or reduction of a financial asset. Which is correct?
column14: Statement I is false because Monetised Deficit refers specifically to government borrowing from the Reserve Bank of India, not the open market. Statement II is the fundamental definition of a capital receipt.

column6: Consider these statements regarding the Indian Constitution: I. Article 21 covers the right to die with dignity by legalizing active euthanasia. II. The Ninth Schedule was added to the Constitution by the First Amendment Act. Which is correct?
column14: Statement I is false because active euthanasia remains illegal in India; only passive euthanasia is permitted under strict guidelines. Statement II is true as the First Amendment introduced the Ninth Schedule.

column6: Consider these statements regarding flagship schemes and economy: I. The PM SVANidhi scheme provides collateral free working capital loans to rural agricultural laborers. II. The Goods and Services Tax is fundamentally a destination based consumption tax. Which is correct?
column14: Statement I is false because the PM SVANidhi scheme targets urban street vendors, not rural agricultural laborers. Statement II is true as GST is a destination based consumption tax.

column6: Consider these statements regarding disaster management: I. A biological disaster like a viral pandemic is legally managed under the Disaster Management Act. II. The National Crisis Management Committee is chaired by the Union Home Minister. Which is correct?
column14: Statement I is true as COVID 19 was officially managed under the DMA 2005. Statement II is false because the National Crisis Management Committee is headed by the Cabinet Secretary.

column6: Consider these statements regarding climate change: I. Methane has a shorter atmospheric lifetime than Carbon Dioxide but a much higher global warming potential. II. The Kyoto Protocol explicitly mandated developing countries like India to cut greenhouse gas emissions. Which is correct?
column14: Statement I is true; methane disappears faster but traps much more heat. Statement II is false because the principle of Common but Differentiated Responsibilities meant developing nations like India had no binding targets under Kyoto.

column6: Consider these statements regarding defence technology: I. The S400 Triumf is an indigenous anti ballistic missile system completely developed by DRDO. II. Project 75 India involves the domestic construction of nuclear powered attack submarines. Which is correct?
column14: Both statements are false. The S400 is a Russian system, not indigenous. Project 75 India involves conventional diesel electric submarines with air independent propulsion, not nuclear submarines.

column6: Consider these statements regarding the Directive Principles of State Policy: I. The Constitution explicitly classifies them into Gandhian Social and Liberal Intellectual categories. II. Laws implementing Article 39 clauses b and c can take precedence over Fundamental Rights 14 and 19. Which is correct?
column14: Statement I is false because the Constitution itself does not classify DPSPs; this classification is done by scholars for study. Statement II is true under Article 31C.

column6: Consider these statements regarding seismic disasters: I. A magnitude 6 earthquake releases exactly double the energy of a magnitude 5 earthquake. II. Liquefaction occurs when water saturated soil temporarily loses its strength during violent shaking. Which is correct?
column14: Statement I is false because a whole number increase on the Richter scale represents about 31.6 times more energy release, not double. Statement II correctly defines liquefaction.

column6: Consider these statements regarding Jammu and Kashmir history: I. The Kalhana Rajatarangini was written during the reign of King Zain ul Abidin. II. The Instrument of Accession was signed by Maharaja Hari Singh on twenty sixth October nineteen forty seven. Which is correct?
column14: Statement I is false because Rajatarangini was written during the reign of Jayasimha, not Zain ul Abidin. Statement II is the correct historical date of accession.

column6: Consider these statements regarding Jammu and Kashmir geography: I. The Kishanganga river is a major right bank tributary of the Jhelum river. II. The Zoji La pass connects the Kashmir Valley with the Jammu region. Which is correct?
column14: Statement I is geographically true. Statement II is false because the Zoji La pass connects the Kashmir Valley with Ladakh, not Jammu.

column6: Consider these statements regarding the JK Reorganisation Act 2019: I. The Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir has retained representation in the Rajya Sabha. II. The Act establishes a separate Public Service Commission exclusively for the Union Territory of Ladakh. Which is correct?
