column6: Why is satellite uplink frequency strictly kept higher than the downlink frequency?
column7: To prevent signal fading from tropospheric ducting
column8: To minimize onboard satellite transmit power requirements
column9: To completely eliminate cosmic background noise
column10: To increase the antenna size on the satellite
column14: Higher frequencies suffer much greater path attenuation. Ground stations possess massive power generators to handle this high uplink loss. Satellites rely on limited solar power, so they transmit the downlink at a lower frequency to strictly conserve power.

column6: The numerical aperture of an optical fiber is 0.5. Find the exact acceptance angle in air.
column14: By definition, the numerical aperture equals the sine of the acceptance angle for a fiber placed in air. The sine inverse of 0.5 is exactly 30 degrees. Light entering outside this cone will not undergo total internal reflection.

column6: Evaluate satellite multiple access techniques: 1. TDMA assigns identical frequency channels to multiple users strictly at different time slots. 2. CDMA separates users purely by assigning strictly distinct frequency bands. Which of the statements given above are correct?
column14: Statement 1 is perfectly true for Time Division Multiple Access. Statement 2 is completely false. CDMA separates users using unique digital spreading codes on the exact same frequency band, whereas FDMA is the technique that assigns distinct frequency bands.

column6: Assertion: Optical fiber systems strictly use light wavelengths around 1550 nanometers for long haul links. Reason: Silica glass exhibits an absolute minimum attenuation specifically at the 1550 nanometer wavelength. Choose the correct option:
column7: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason explains Assertion
column8: Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason does not explain Assertion
column9: Assertion is true but Reason is false
column10: Both Assertion and Reason are completely false
column14: Both statements are absolutely true. Modern long distance telecommunications operate in the third transmission window at 1550 nanometers because standard silica glass fibers hit their absolute lowest optical loss specifically at this wavelength.

column6: A satellite orbit semi major axis is increased by exactly four times. How does the orbital time period change?
column14: Kepler third law strictly dictates that the square of the orbital period is proportional to the cube of the semi major axis. Cubing the factor of four gives 64. The square root of 64 gives exactly eight, meaning the period increases eightfold.

column6: Consider optical fiber classifications: 1. Graded index fibers have a strictly uniform refractive index throughout the entire core. 2. Graded index fibers significantly reduce modal dispersion compared to multimode step index fibers. Which of the statements given above are correct?
column14: Statement 1 is false. Graded index fibers have a core index that is highest at the center and gradually decreases toward the cladding. This parabolic profile continuously bends light, making Statement 2 true because it equalizes the transit time of different modes.

column6: Assertion: A highly directive satellite antenna creates a massive global coverage footprint on Earth. Reason: High directivity strictly requires concentrating the radiated electromagnetic power into an extremely narrow spot beam. Choose the correct option:
column7: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason explains Assertion
column8: Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason does not explain Assertion
column9: Assertion is true but Reason is false
column10: Assertion is false but Reason is true
column14: The Reason is mathematically true. High directivity concentrates energy into a very tight, narrow beam. Consequently, the Assertion is completely false. A narrow beam inherently produces a much smaller footprint, known as a spot beam, rather than massive global coverage.

column6: Consider standard transport layer header characteristics: 1. Minimum TCP header size is exactly 20 bytes. 2. Minimum UDP header size is exactly 8 bytes. Which of the statements given above are correct?
column14: Both statements are strictly true. TCP requires a minimum of 20 bytes to handle sequence numbers and acknowledgments. UDP is connectionless and lightweight, requiring only 8 bytes for source port, destination port, length, and checksum.

column6: Assertion: An IPv4 router strictly modifies the source and destination IP addresses during packet forwarding. Reason: Routers operate at the network layer to connect completely distinct subnets. Choose the correct option:

column8: Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason does not explain Assertion

column6: Identify the exact Protocol Data Unit name strictly used at the OSI transport layer.
column14: At the data link layer the unit is a Frame. At the network layer it is a Datagram or Packet. At the transport layer, data is chopped into manageable pieces specifically called Segments.

column6: Evaluate the original four layer TCP IP model architecture: 1. It strictly integrates OSI presentation and session functions into the application layer. 2. It specifically defines a dedicated physical layer for hardware specifications. Which of the statements given above are correct?
column14: Statement 1 is true as the TCP IP application layer absorbs the top three OSI layers. Statement 2 is completely false because the original TCP IP model relies on a broad Network Access layer and lacks any dedicated physical hardware layer specification.

column6: Transmission time is 100 milliseconds and propagation delay is 50 milliseconds. Find exact Stop and Wait link utilization efficiency.
column14: Link efficiency equals transmission time divided by the sum of transmission time plus twice the propagation delay. Twice 50 is 100. Adding 100 and 100 gives 200. Dividing 100 by 200 yields exactly 0.5 or 50 percent.

column6: Assertion: The TCP slow start phase strictly increases the congestion window linearly. Reason: TCP avoids network collapse by probing available bandwidth extremely cautiously. Choose the correct option:
column7: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason explains Assertion
column8: Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason does not explain Assertion
column9: Assertion is true but Reason is false
column10: Assertion is false but Reason is true
column14: The Reason is true as TCP probes networks to prevent congestion. The Assertion is a classic trap and completely false. Despite its misleading name, the slow start phase actually increases the congestion window exponentially, not linearly.

column6: Consider the operation of the Address Resolution Protocol: 1. The initial ARP request is strictly broadcast over the local subnet. 2. The subsequent ARP reply is strictly unicast back to the original sender. Which of the statements given above are correct?
column14: Both statements are true. A device broadcasts an ARP request asking who owns a specific IP address. The target machine recognizes its own IP and sends the MAC address reply directly back to the sender via a targeted unicast message.

column6: An IPv4 router fragments a packet into maximum payloads of exactly 1480 bytes. Find the exact fragment offset value for the second fragment.
column14: The fragment offset field strictly measures data in scaled units of eight bytes. The first fragment carries the first 1480 payload bytes. Dividing 1480 by exactly 8 yields a fragment offset value of 185 for the start of the second fragment.

column6: Which specific OSI layer is strictly responsible for mapping logical port numbers to active end user software processes?
column14: The Network layer routes data to the correct destination machine using IP addresses. The Transport layer uses port numbers to multiplex and demultiplex the data, ensuring it reaches the exact software process running on that machine.

column6: Evaluate standard Internet Protocol and Transmission Control Protocol checksum operations: 1. The IPv4 checksum strictly protects both the network header and the data payload. 2. The TCP checksum strictly covers the transport header, data payload, and a pseudo header. Which of the statements given above are correct?
column14: Statement 1 is completely false. The IPv4 checksum is calculated strictly over the network header fields to save processing time at routers. Statement 2 is true because the TCP checksum provides end to end reliability by verifying the transport header, data payload, and a pseudo network header.

column6: A subnet is configured with a CIDR notation of slash 28. Find the exact number of usable host IP addresses available.
column14: A slash 28 subnet strictly leaves 4 bits for host addresses. Two to the power of four is 16. Subtracting the network address and broadcast address leaves exactly 14 usable host IPs.

column6: A host has the IP address 192.168.1.130 with a slash 26 subnet mask. Identify the exact network address.
column14: A slash 26 mask gives exactly 2 bits for subnets in the fourth octet, creating a block size of 64. The subnets start at 0, 64, 128, and 192. The address 130 falls strictly inside the block starting precisely at 192.168.1.128.

column6: Four contiguous slash 24 networks need to be completely aggregated into a single routing table entry. Find the new aggregated CIDR prefix.
column14: Aggregating exactly four contiguous slash 24 networks requires borrowing two bits from the network portion back into the host portion. Subtracting two from 24 yields a strictly aggregated slash 22 prefix.

column10: Assertion is false but Reason is true

column6: Evaluate the standard use of the IP address 255.255.255.255: 1. It acts as a strict limited broadcast directed only to hosts on the same local subnet. 2. A local router will automatically forward this packet to external networks. Which of the statements given above are correct?
column14: Statement 1 is perfectly true as this address targets all local hosts. Statement 2 is completely false because routers strictly block limited broadcast packets to prevent massive network traffic storms.

column6: A Class B network requires at least 50 subnets with 1000 hosts each. Find the required subnet mask.
column14: Creating 50 subnets requires borrowing 6 bits from the host portion. This leaves 10 bits for hosts, allowing 1022 usable hosts. Adding the 6 borrowed bits to the default 16 bit mask gives a 22 bit mask, which is exactly 255.255.252.0.

column6: A router routing table contains entries for 10.1.0.0 slash 16 and 10.1.2.0 slash 24. A packet arrives for destination 10.1.2.10. How will it be routed?

column8: Sent to the slash 24 route strictly

column6: Host A is 10.1.1.20 slash 27 and Host B is 10.1.1.40 slash 27. Evaluate their connectivity: 1. They belong to the exact same local subnet. 2. They strictly require a router to communicate. Which of the statements given above are correct?
column14: A slash 27 mask creates a block size of 32. Host A falls in the first subnet from 0 to 31. Host B falls in the second subnet from 32 to 63. Since they are on completely different subnets, Statement 1 is false and Statement 2 is true.

column6: The allocated network address is 172.16.32.0 slash 20. Find the exact last usable host IP address in this specific subnet.

column6: Path loss exponent is strictly four. How does received power change if distance doubles?
column14: Received power Pr is proportional to 1 / d^n where n = 4. New distance is 2 * d. New power is proportional to 1 / 2^4 * d^4. Since 2^4 = 16, the new power is exactly 1 / 16 of the original power.

column6: Evaluate guard channel strategies: 1. They reserve channels exclusively for new incoming calls. 2. They prioritize handoff requests to prevent call drops. Which of the statements given above are correct?

column6: RIP strictly limits the maximum valid hop count to what exact number?
column14: RIP defines infinity as 16 hops to strictly prevent infinite routing loops. Therefore, the maximum valid hop count for a reachable destination network is exactly 15.

column6: Consider the underlying algorithms for routing protocols: 1. RIP strictly uses Dijkstra algorithm. 2. OSPF strictly uses Bellman Ford algorithm. Which of the statements given above are correct?
column14: Both statements are completely false. RIP is a distance vector protocol relying purely on the Bellman Ford algorithm. OSPF is a link state protocol that strictly uses the Dijkstra shortest path first algorithm.

column6: A router interface has a bandwidth of exactly 10 Mbps. Find the standard OSPF cost.
column14: OSPF cost = Reference Bandwidth / Interface Bandwidth. Step 1: Default Reference Bandwidth = 10^8 bps. Step 2: Interface Bandwidth = 10 Mbps = 10^7 bps. Step 3: Cost = 10^8 / 10^7 = 10.

column6: Assertion: OSPF encapsulates its routing updates strictly inside UDP datagrams. Reason: UDP provides lightweight connectionless transport ideal for fast routing convergence. Choose the correct option:
column7: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason explains Assertion
column8: Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason does not explain Assertion
column9: Assertion is true but Reason is false
column10: Assertion is false but Reason is true

column6: What is the strict primary purpose of the split horizon rule in RIP?
column8: To prevent two node routing loops
column9: To divide large autonomous systems into areas
column14: Split horizon strictly prevents a router from advertising a route back out the exact same interface it was learned from. This mathematical rule completely prevents basic two node routing loops.

column6: Evaluate standard OSPF area design: 1. All OSPF areas must strictly connect physically or logically to Area 0. 2. Area 0 serves as the absolute backbone area. Which of the statements given above are correct?
column14: Both statements are true. OSPF relies on a strict two tier hierarchy where Area 0 is the backbone. All other non backbone areas must directly connect to Area 0 to route traffic properly.

column6: Assertion: RIP converges significantly faster than OSPF after a network topology change. Reason: RIP only sends updates to immediate neighbors while OSPF floods updates network wide. Choose the correct option:

column8: Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason does not explain Assertion
column9: Assertion is true but Reason is false
column10: Assertion is false but Reason is true

column6: Which OSPF packet type is strictly used to discover and maintain neighbor relationships?
column14: OSPF routers strictly multicast Hello packets at regular intervals. These specific packets dynamically discover new local neighbors and act as keepalives to maintain existing adjacencies.

column6: What is the default periodic update timer for RIP routing tables?
column14: By default, a RIP router strictly broadcasts its entire routing table out all active RIP interfaces every 30 seconds, regardless of whether the network topology has actually changed or not.

column6: Consider OSPF routing knowledge: 1. Every router maintains a complete topological map of its own area. 2. Routers strictly rely on neighbors for path selection without knowing the full topology. Which of the statements given above are correct?
column14: Statement 1 is perfectly true because OSPF is a link state protocol where each router builds a complete shortest path tree. Statement 2 describes distance vector protocols like RIP and is therefore completely false for OSPF.

column6: Evaluate Pitcher plant nutrition: 1. It is purely heterotrophic. 2. It digests insects strictly for nitrogen. Which of the statements given above are correct?

column6: Consider plant transport mechanisms: 1. Root pressure pushes water to the absolute top of tall trees. 2. Xylem transport is strictly unidirectional. Which of the statements given above are correct?
column14: Root pressure only pushes water short distances. Transpiration pull lifts water in tall trees. Xylem flow strictly moves upward from roots to leaves.

column6: A single glucose molecule undergoes glycolysis. Find the exact net ATP yield.

column8: To mandate the daily sanitization of all physical currency in bank vaults.
column9: To strictly withdraw soiled or mutilated currency notes and supply fresh ones.
column10: To ensure all printed notes strictly utilize environmentally friendly green ink.
column14: The Clean Note Policy strictly aims to provide good quality currency notes and coins to the citizens while continuously withdrawing soiled and torn notes from active circulation.

column6: Consider the following statements about the commencement and structure of the Act: I. The J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019 came into effect on 31st October 2019. II. It reorganized the state into two Union Territories, both having their own separate Legislative Assemblies. Which is correct?
column14: Statement II is false because the Union Territory of Ladakh was created without a legislature, whereas the UT of J&K was created with a legislature.

column6: Consider the following statements regarding the bicameral legislature of the erstwhile state: I. The Act formally abolished the Legislative Council (Upper House) of Jammu and Kashmir. II. All bills pending in the Legislative Council lapsed immediately upon the abolition of the Council. Which is correct?
column14: Under Section 57 of the Act, the Legislative Council was abolished and all bills pending in the Council lapsed on the appointed day.

column6: Consider the following statements regarding the Judiciary under the Act: I. The Act established two separate High Courts for the UT of J&K and the UT of Ladakh. II. The judges of the former High Court of J&K automatically became the judges of the High Court for the new UTs. Which is correct?
column14: Statement I is false. Section 75 states that there shall be a common High Court for both the UT of Jammu and Kashmir and the UT of Ladakh.

column6: Consider the following statements about representation in the Parliament of India: I. The UT of Jammu and Kashmir is allocated 5 seats in the Lok Sabha. II. The UT of Ladakh is allocated 1 seat in the Rajya Sabha. Which is correct?
column14: Statement II is false. Ladakh has 1 seat in the Lok Sabha but 0 seats in the Rajya Sabha. J&K retains 4 seats in the Rajya Sabha.

column6: Consider the following statements regarding the Legislative Assembly seats for Pakistan Occupied Jammu & Kashmir (PoJK): I. 24 seats in the Legislative Assembly of the UT of J&K remain vacant for areas under the occupation of Pakistan. II. These 24 vacant seats are not taken into account for calculating the total membership of the Assembly for government formation. Which is correct?
column14: Under Section 14, 24 seats are reserved for PoJK. They remain vacant and are excluded when calculating the quorum or majority needed to form a government.

column6: Consider the following statements regarding the legislative powers of the J&K Assembly: I. The subjects of 'Police' and 'Public Order' fall under the legislative jurisdiction of the J&K Assembly. II. The subject of 'Land' is completely excluded from the jurisdiction of the J&K Legislative Assembly. Which is correct?
column14: Both are false. Under Section 32, the Assembly can make laws on any matter in the State List EXCEPT "Police" and "Public Order". Unlike Delhi, "Land" remains under the domain of the J&K Assembly.

column6: Consider the following statements regarding the Lieutenant Governor (LG): I. The Lieutenant Governor of the UT of J&K is appointed by the President of India. II. The LG has the power to promulgate ordinances during the recess of the Legislative Assembly. Which is correct?
column14: Both statements are true. The President appoints the LG (Article 239) and Section 52 of the Act grants the LG ordinance-making powers when the assembly is not in session.

column6: Consider the following statements regarding the application of laws: I. According to the Act, all Central Laws listed in the Fifth Schedule were made applicable to the UTs of J&K and Ladakh. II. The Indian Penal Code (IPC) officially replaced the Ranbir Penal Code (RPC). Which is correct?
column14: The Fifth Schedule of the Act made over 100 central laws explicitly applicable, and formally repealed state-specific laws like the RPC, replacing it with the IPC.

column6: Consider the following statements regarding political reservations: I. The Act provides for the reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes (SC) and Scheduled Tribes (ST) in the Legislative Assembly of J&K. II. The reservation of these seats is strictly based on the proportion of their population to the total population of the UT. Which is correct?
column14: Under Section 14(6), seats are reserved for SCs and STs, and the number bears the same proportion to total seats as their population bears to the total population of the UT.

column6: Consider the following statements regarding the division of assets and liabilities: I. The Act mandated the Central Government to appoint Advisory Committees for the apportionment of assets, rights, and liabilities. II. These committees were tasked with managing disputes over assets strictly between the newly formed UT of Ladakh and the neighboring state of Himachal Pradesh. Which is correct?
column14: Statement II is false. The Advisory Committees (Sections 84 and 85) were appointed to apportion the assets and liabilities of the former State of J&K between the two new UTs (J&K and Ladakh), not with Himachal Pradesh.

column6: Convert 0.625₁₀ to base 2.
column14: 0.625 * 2 = 1.25, record 1. 0.25 * 2 = 0.50, record 0. 0.50 * 2 = 1.0, record 1. Reading integers top to bottom strictly gives 0.101₂.

column6: Convert 3E₁₆ to base 8.
column14: 3E₁₆ = 00111110₂. Grouping these binary bits into threes from right to left gives 000 111 110. Converting these exact groups to octal strictly yields 76₈.

column6: Find the exact 2s complement of 101100₂.
column14: Find the 1s complement by perfectly inverting all bits to get 010011₂. Add exactly 1 to the lowest order bit to get 010100₂.

column6: If 324ₓ = 89₁₀ find the exact numerical value of x.
column14: The algebraic equation is 3 * x² + 2 * x + 4 = 89. This simplifies strictly to the quadratic equation 3x² + 2x - 85 = 0. Solving this completely yields a positive integer root x = 5.

column6: Evaluate 132₈ - 45₈.
column14: Base 8 subtraction. First column 2 - 5 requires a borrow. Borrowing 1 strictly adds 8, making 10 - 5 = 5. Second column remaining 2 - 4 requires borrow, making 10 - 4 = 6. Final result is 65₈.

column6: Evaluate A9₁₆ + 5B₁₆.
column14: Base 16 addition. 9 + B = 9 + 11 = 20₁₀. 20 - 16 strictly leaves 4 with a carry of 1. A + 5 + 1 = 10 + 5 + 1 = 16₁₀. 16 - 16 strictly leaves 0 with a carry of 1. Final result is 104₁₆.

column6: Convert 2000₁₀ to base 16.
column14: 2000 / 16 = 125 remainder 0. 125 / 16 = 7 remainder 13 which is exactly D. 7 / 16 = 0 remainder 7. Reading remainders bottom to top strictly gives 7D0₁₆.

column6: Find the exact minimum number of bits required to perfectly represent 850₁₀ in base 2.
column14: The maximum value for 9 bits is 2⁹ - 1 = 511. The maximum value for 10 bits is 2¹⁰ - 1 = 1023. Since 850 perfectly falls between these, it strictly requires 10 bits.

column6: Evaluate 1011₂ * 101₂.
column14: 1011₂ = 11₁₀. 101₂ = 5₁₀. 11 * 5 = 55₁₀. Converting 55 back to binary strictly yields 32 + 16 + 4 + 2 + 1 = 110111₂.

column6: Convert 1101.11₂ to base 10.
column14: The integer part 1101₂ = 8 + 4 + 0 + 1 = 13₁₀. The fractional part .11₂ = 1/2 + 1/4 = 0.50 + 0.25 = 0.75₁₀. Combining them strictly yields 13.75₁₀.

column6: Evaluate these core data structure statements. 1. Stacks strictly follow Last In First Out logic. 2. Queues strictly follow First In First Out logic. 3. Priority queues strictly require a sorted array implementation. Choose the correct option.
column14: Stacks operate strictly on LIFO and Queues on FIFO. However, statement 3 is completely false because priority queues are most efficiently implemented using a Heap data structure, not a strictly sorted array, to guarantee logarithmic time insertions.

column6: Identify the strictly incorrect statement regarding binary trees.
column7: Complete binary trees lack right leaning empty spaces.
column8: Full binary trees mandate exactly zero or two children.
column9: Perfect binary trees have perfectly even bottom levels.
column10: Degenerate binary trees optimally support fast binary searches.
column14: Statement D is completely false. A degenerate binary tree has every parent possessing exactly one child, making it structurally identical to a simple linked list. Consequently, searching it degrades strictly to order N time, completely ruining binary search capabilities.

column6: Match the sorting algorithms with their worst case time. List 1: 1 Quick Sort, 2 Merge Sort, 3 Selection Sort. List 2: X order N log N, Y order N², Z order N³. Choose the exact correct matching.

column14: Quick Sort degrades terribly to order N² when the pivot is extremely poor. Selection Sort always takes order N² regardless of the input array. Merge Sort is highly reliable, strictly guaranteeing order N log N time in every single worst case scenario.

column6: Evaluate these statements about graph traversal algorithms. 1. Depth First Search utilizes a stack data structure. 2. Breadth First Search utilizes a queue data structure. 3. Dijkstra algorithm works perfectly on negative weight edges. Choose the correct option.
column14: DFS uses a stack and BFS uses a queue, making statements 1 and 2 perfectly accurate. Statement 3 is entirely false because the Dijkstra algorithm strictly fails on negative weight edges, as its greedy approach permanently locks paths assuming costs always increase.

column6: Evaluate these hashing collision resolution statements. 1. Linear probing frequently causes severe primary clustering issues. 2. Quadratic probing completely eliminates all secondary clustering issues. 3. Separate chaining handles load factors strictly above 1. Choose the correct option.
column14: Linear probing creates large primary clusters. Separate chaining uses attached linked lists, safely allowing load factors above 1. However, statement 2 is false because while quadratic probing stops primary clustering, it still strictly suffers from secondary clustering.

column6: Match the data structures with their optimal applications. List 1: 1 Trie, 2 Graph, 3 Stack. List 2: X Network routing, Y Function call recursion, Z Dictionary word search. Choose the exact correct matching.

column14: A Trie is mathematically optimized specifically for prefix and dictionary word searches. Graphs provide the fundamental associative structure for mapping complex network routing. Stacks are universally utilized by system compilers to strictly track function call recursion.

column6: Evaluate these statements regarding linked list operations. 1. Singly linked lists allow strictly backward node traversal. 2. Doubly linked lists consume more memory per node. 3. Circular linked lists lack a strict null pointer. Choose the correct option.
column14: Doubly linked lists require extra memory for the previous pointer. Circular linked lists strictly point the tail back to the head, eliminating null terminators. Statement 1 is totally false because singly linked lists strictly permit only forward traversal.

column6: Identify the strictly incorrect dynamic programming statement.
column7: Memoization strictly follows a top down recursive approach.
column8: Tabulation strictly follows a bottom up iterative approach.
column9: Optimal substructure is strictly mandatory for dynamic programming.
column10: Dynamic programming completely ignores overlapping subproblem state constraints.
column14: Statement D is absolutely false. Dynamic programming derives its entire algorithmic efficiency strictly by remembering and reusing the computed solutions to overlapping subproblems. Ignoring these states would instantly reduce it to a horribly slow naive recursive algorithm.

column6: Match these standard algorithms with their strict paradigms. List 1: 1 Binary Search, 2 Kruskal Algorithm, 3 Bellman Ford. List 2: X Greedy Method, Y Dynamic Programming, Z Divide and Conquer. Choose the exact correct matching.
column7: 1 is X, 2 is Y, 3 is Z

column10: 1 is Z, 2 is Y, 3 is X
column14: Binary Search strictly divides the search space in half. Kruskal Algorithm greedily selects the absolute minimum weight edge to build a spanning tree. Bellman Ford strictly uses dynamic programming to relax all graph edges sequentially.

column6: Evaluate these statements regarding heap data structures. 1. Max heaps guarantee the root is the maximum element. 2. Building a heap iteratively takes order N² time. 3. Heap sort requires strictly order N auxiliary memory. Choose the correct option.
column14: Max heaps strictly place the maximum element at the root, making statement 1 true. Statement 2 is false because the optimal bottom up build heap operation strictly takes order N time. Statement 3 is false because Heap sort is an in place algorithm requiring strictly order 1 auxiliary memory.

column6: Match these CPU scheduling algorithms with their primary characteristics. List 1: 1 Round Robin, 2 Shortest Job First, 3 First Come First Serve. List 2: X Time quantum driven, Y Convoy effect prone, Z Minimum average waiting. Choose the exact correct matching.
column7: 1 is X, 2 is Y, 3 is Z

column10: 1 is Z, 2 is Y, 3 is X
column14: Round Robin strictly utilizes a repeating time quantum to preempt processes. Shortest Job First mathematically guarantees the absolute minimum average waiting time. First Come First Serve strictly suffers from the convoy effect where short processes wait behind massive ones.

column6: Evaluate these statements regarding process deadlock conditions. 1. Mutual exclusion is mandatory for deadlock occurrence. 2. Hold and wait guarantees a deadlock situation. 3. Bankers algorithm strictly performs deadlock avoidance. Choose the correct option.
column14: Mutual exclusion is one of the four strictly required conditions. However, statement 2 is entirely false because hold and wait is merely a prerequisite, it does not guarantee a deadlock without circular wait. Bankers algorithm strictly avoids deadlocks by simulating safe states.

column6: Identify the strictly incorrect statement regarding memory management techniques.
column7: Paging completely eliminates severe external fragmentation.
column8: Segmentation completely eliminates severe internal fragmentation.
column9: Paging divides logical memory into variable sizes.
column10: Segmentation divides memory based on user perspective.
column14: Statement C is completely false. Paging strictly divides physical memory into fixed size frames and logical memory into identically fixed size pages. Segmentation is the technique that utilizes variable sizes based strictly on the user perspective of program modules.

column6: Evaluate these statements regarding virtual memory and thrashing. 1. Thrashing strictly occurs due to excessive page faults. 2. Increasing multiprogramming degree always reduces system thrashing. 3. Working set model strictly prevents system thrashing. Choose the correct option.
column14: Thrashing happens when the CPU spends strictly more time swapping pages than executing processes. Statement 2 is absolutely false because continuously increasing the multiprogramming degree eventually starves processes of frames, directly causing violent thrashing. The working set model allocates enough frames to strictly prevent this.

column6: Match the file system allocation methods with their drawbacks. List 1: 1 Contiguous allocation, 2 Linked allocation, 3 Indexed allocation. List 2: X Suffers severe external fragmentation, Y Requires strict sequential access, Z Centralizes all block pointers together. Choose the exact correct matching.

column8: 1 is Y, 2 is X, 3 is Z
column9: 1 is X, 2 is Z, 3 is Y

column14: Contiguous allocation physically groups files together, inevitably causing severe external fragmentation. Linked allocation scatters blocks using internal pointers, strictly ruining direct random access. Indexed allocation strictly centralizes all pointers into a single specific index block for instantaneous direct access.

column6: Identify the strictly incorrect statement regarding process synchronization.
column7: Binary semaphores are strictly identical to mutex locks.
column8: Counting semaphores strictly manage multiple resource instances.
column9: Wait operation strictly decrements the semaphore integer value.
column10: Signal operation strictly wakes up waiting blocked processes.
column14: Statement A is a classic competitive exam trap. While conceptually similar, they are absolutely not identical. A mutex lock strictly possesses an ownership property meaning only the specific thread that acquired it can release it. Binary semaphores lack this strict ownership constraint completely.

column6: Match the page replacement algorithms with their fundamental behaviors. List 1: 1 Belady Anomaly, 2 Least Recently Used, 3 Optimal Replacement. List 2: X Looks strictly backward in time, Y Strictly requires future knowledge, Z Occurs strictly in FIFO algorithms. Choose the exact correct matching.

column8: 1 is Z, 2 is X, 3 is Y
column9: 1 is X, 2 is Y, 3 is Z

column14: Belady Anomaly is a strict paradox where adding more physical frames increases page faults, happening exclusively in FIFO. Least Recently Used makes decisions strictly looking backward at historical access. Optimal Replacement strictly requires mathematically impossible future clairvoyance to discard the latest needed page.

column6: Evaluate these statements regarding Unix inode architecture. 1. Inodes strictly contain actual user file data. 2. Inodes strictly store file permission and ownership metadata. 3. Inodes strictly utilize direct and indirect memory pointers. Choose the correct option.
column14: Statement 1 is completely false. Inodes are purely metadata structures. They strictly never store the actual user file data, but rather they store the permissions, timestamps, ownership, and the complex hierarchical pointers required to physically locate the data blocks on the disk.

column6: Identify the strictly incorrect statement regarding CPU context switching.
column7: Context switching strictly requires hardware interrupt intervention.
column8: Process control blocks strictly store saved CPU states.
column9: Context switch time is completely productive CPU work.
column10: Thread switching is strictly faster than process switching.
column14: Statement C is entirely false. Context switching time is pure system overhead. During the strict process of saving the old state into the PCB and loading the new state, the CPU performs absolutely zero productive user level execution.

column6: Evaluate these statements regarding the Translation Lookaside Buffer. 1. TLB strictly acts as a high speed hardware memory cache. 2. TLB strictly stores recently translated page table entries. 3. TLB misses strictly cause fatal system kernel panics. Choose the correct option.
column14: The TLB is an associative hardware cache strictly designed to speed up virtual to physical address translations. However, statement 3 is completely false. A TLB miss simply forces the system to perform a slightly slower standard page walk in main memory, it never causes a fatal panic.

column6: Evaluate these statements regarding common malware behavior types. 1. Spyware strictly monitors user activity continuously and covertly. 2. Adware strictly encrypts user files for massive ransom. 3. Trojans strictly disguise themselves as highly legitimate software. Choose the correct option.
column14: Spyware silently tracks user data and Trojans trick users by looking like safe programs. However, statement 2 is completely false because encrypting files for financial extortion is strictly the defining characteristic of Ransomware, whereas Adware simply displays unwanted advertisements.

column6: Match the specific social engineering attacks with their vectors. List 1: 1 Phishing, 2 Vishing, 3 Smishing. List 2: X SMS text manipulation, Y Fraudulent voice calls, Z Deceptive email spoofing. Choose the exact correct matching.

column8: Ransomware secretly utilizes hardware for covert cryptocurrency mining.
column9: Spear phishing targets highly specific individual corporate victims.
column10: Whaling strictly targets high ranking executive corporate officers.
column14: Statement B is completely false. Secretly stealing a victims CPU power to mine digital currency is strictly known as Cryptojacking. Ransomware relies exclusively on locking files or systems and openly demanding payment to restore user access.

column6: Evaluate these statements regarding complex network cyber attacks. 1. DDoS attacks strictly utilize multiple compromised zombie machines. 2. Botnets strictly operate under remote attacker command control. 3. Man in the middle attackers strictly intercept network communications. Choose the correct option.
column14: All three statements are perfectly accurate. Distributed Denial of Service floods servers using armies of infected computers called Botnets, which strictly await commands from remote attackers. Man in the middle attacks covertly intercept and relay messages between two unaware communicating parties.

Worms are highly dangerous because unlike standard viruses, they strictly self replicate across networks without needing a host file. Logic bombs lie completely dormant until a specific date or user action triggers them.

column7: Keyloggers covertly record every single physical keyboard stroke.
column8: Polymorphic malware strictly alters its internal code signature continually.
column9: Fileless malware strictly leaves massive executable files safely behind.
column10: Pharming strictly redirects users to completely fraudulent website addresses.
column14: Statement C is entirely false. Fileless malware is incredibly dangerous specifically because it operates entirely within the volatile system memory RAM. column6: Evaluate these statements regarding cyber defense and vulnerabilities. 1. Zero day exploits strictly target entirely unknown software vulnerabilities. 2. Social engineering strictly exploits human psychological manipulation vulnerabilities. 3. Antivirus software perfectly prevents zero day exploits completely permanently. Choose the correct option.
column14: Statements 1 and 2 accurately define zero day attacks and social engineering. Statement 3 is absolutely false because traditional signature based antivirus software cannot mathematically stop a zero day exploit, as the malicious signature is strictly unknown to the cybersecurity community.

column6: Identify the strictly incorrect statement regarding authentication breach attempts.
column7: Dictionary attacks strictly try common known password word combinations.
column8: Brute force strictly attempts every possible character sequence combination.
column9: Credential stuffing strictly reuses stolen passwords across multiple sites.
column10: Two factor authentication completely eliminates phishing risks forever entirely.

Scareware uses extreme psychological manipulation to trick users into buying fake antivirus software.

column6: Evaluate these statements regarding specialized network spoofing attacks. 1. IP spoofing strictly masks the true origin network address. 2. MAC spoofing strictly alters the physical hardware network identity. 3. DNS spoofing strictly corrupts the domain name resolution cache. Choose the correct option.
column14: All three statements strictly define their respective attacks perfectly. IP spoofing hides the sender, MAC spoofing impersonates a trusted physical machine on a local network, and DNS spoofing poisons the cache to secretly redirect legitimate web traffic to malicious IP addresses.

column6: Evaluate these statements regarding fundamental firewall inspection types. 1. Stateful firewalls strictly inspect active connection session tables. 2. Stateless firewalls strictly evaluate individual packets in total isolation. 3. Packet filtering firewalls deeply inspect application layer payload data. Choose the correct option.
column14: Statements 1 and 2 are perfectly accurate regarding stateful and stateless behavior. Statement 3 is entirely false because simple packet filtering firewalls strictly evaluate only layer three and layer four network headers, completely ignoring the application payload data.

column6: Identify the strictly incorrect statement regarding intrusion security systems.
column7: IDS strictly operates passively out of the network band.
column8: IPS strictly sits inline to intercept malicious network traffic.
column9: Network firewalls strictly prevent all internal insider threat attacks.
column10: Both systems strictly utilize identical traffic inspection detection engines.
column14: Statement C is completely false. Network firewalls are strictly designed as perimeter defense mechanisms to block external threats. They are generally blind and powerless against malicious insider threats already operating safely behind the firewall perimeter.

column6: Match the intrusion detection methodologies with their exact behaviors. List 1: 1 Signature Based, 2 Anomaly Based, 3 Heuristic Based. List 2: X Flags deviations from established normal system baselines, Y Strictly identifies entirely unknown novel zero day attacks, Z Compares traffic against known malicious byte sequence patterns. column14: Signature based detection strictly matches known bad patterns just like traditional antivirus. Anomaly based detection creates a normal baseline and flags odd deviations. Heuristic based detection strictly evaluates code behavior dynamically to identify entirely novel zero day threats.

column6: Evaluate these statements regarding network versus host detection systems. 1. HIDS strictly monitors internal operating system log modifications. 2. NIDS strictly analyzes encrypted payload traffic without decryption keys. 3. NIDS strictly operates by mirroring traffic from network switches. Choose the correct option.
column14: Host based systems strictly monitor local OS files, and Network based systems strictly utilize spanned switch ports for traffic mirroring. Statement 2 is absolutely false because NIDS cannot mathematically inspect encrypted payloads without strictly possessing the correct decryption keys.

column8: Internal networks strictly sit safely behind the inner firewall.

column14: Statement C is completely false. Public facing web servers strictly reside within the Demilitarized Zone. Placing them inside the highly protected internal intranet would completely expose the most sensitive corporate network segments directly to external internet threats.

Next Generation Firewalls strictly integrate traditional firewall duties with advanced deep packet inspection and active intrusion prevention systems.

column6: Evaluate these statements regarding detection accuracy and error rates. 1. False positives strictly block entirely legitimate benign network traffic. 2. False negatives strictly allow actual malicious attacks to succeed. 3. Highly strict rules completely eliminate all false positive alerts. Choose the correct option.
column14: Statements 1 and 2 perfectly define the two fundamental error types in security systems. Statement 3 is entirely false because implementing highly strict security rules actually increases the volume of false positive alerts by wrongly flagging unusual but benign traffic.

column8: Honeypots strictly generate massive volumes of false positive alerts.

column10: Intruders interacting with honeypots strictly provide valuable threat intelligence.

column6: Evaluate these statements regarding common firewall evasion techniques. 1. IP fragmentation strictly evades simplistic stateless packet filtering firewalls. 2. Traffic obfuscation strictly encodes payloads to bypass signature detection. 3. Source routing strictly forces packets through specific trusted paths. Choose the correct option.

Obfuscation mathematically alters the code signature. Source routing allows attackers to strictly dictate the network path to bypass specific firewall nodes.
